items.title: Feature: add cron-scoped default LLM model/provider configuration
items.body:
## Feature Description

Add a cron-scoped default LLM configuration so scheduled jobs can use a dedicated model/provider by default, while interactive chats keep the profile's main model.

Proposed config shape:

```yaml
cron:
  model: <cron-default-model>
  llm_provider: <cron-default-provider>
  base_url: <optional-cron-base-url>
```

Suggested resolution order for cron agent runs:

```text
job.model/provider/base_url
→ cron.model/llm_provider/base_url
→ HERMES_MODEL / profile model.default and model.provider
```

`cron.provider` already refers to the scheduler/trigger provider, so a distinct key such as `cron.llm_provider` would avoid ambiguity.

## Motivation

Scheduled jobs often need a cheaper or faster model than the main interactive model. Today, users can either change the profile-wide default model or set per-job `model` and `provider` overrides across every cron job.

A cron-scoped default would make cost control easier for users who run many scheduled jobs:

- Interactive chats can use a high-capability model.
- Routine scheduled jobs can use a cheaper model.
- Per-job overrides remain available for high-priority jobs.
- New cron jobs inherit the cron-specific default automatically.

## Current Behavior

Docs and implementation indicate the current cron model routing is:

```text
job.model → HERMES_MODEL → config.yaml model.default
job.provider → profile/global runtime provider resolution
```

Relevant implementation areas:

- `cron/scheduler.py` resolves the model from `job.model`, `HERMES_MODEL`, then `config.yaml model.default`.
- `cron/scheduler.py` resolves runtime provider with `resolve_runtime_provider(requested=job.get("provider"))`.
- `cron/jobs.py` snapshots unpinned provider/model axes for drift detection.
- Current docs state unpinned jobs follow the global default selected by `hermes model`.

## Proposed Solution

1. Add cron-scoped LLM config keys, for example:

```yaml
cron:
  model: gpt-4.1-mini
  llm_provider: openrouter
  base_url: null
```

2. Update cron run resolution to use cron defaults when a job has no explicit override.

3. Keep existing per-job override semantics as highest priority.

4. Integrate with the existing provider/model drift guard:
   - Jobs with explicit per-job fields stay pinned to those fields.
   - Jobs with cron-scoped defaults can snapshot the cron-scoped defaults.
   - If cron-scoped defaults change, the scheduler can apply the same fail-closed behavior already used for global default drift, or provide an explicit “track cron default” mode.

5. Document the distinction clearly:

```yaml
cron.provider      # scheduler provider / trigger backend
cron.llm_provider  # LLM provider used by cron agent runs
```

## Related Issues

This request complements existing cron model/provider work:

- #47019 — per-cron `model` override behavior
- #49046 — cron job provider/model override behavior
- #27530 — resetting per-job model/provider overrides back to default
- #19615 — distinguishing global vs pinned model configuration
- #39196 — inherit main model mode
- #12658 — named model entities

This issue focuses on a profile-level cron default for all unpinned cron jobs.

items.body:
## Summary

`rcedit@5.0.2` — used in `apps/desktop/scripts/set-exe-identity.cjs` to stamp the Hermes icon + version metadata onto `Hermes.exe` — is deprecated and **no longer supported** by its maintainer. Every `npm install` in `apps/desktop` prints:

```
npm warn deprecated rcedit@5.0.2: Package no longer supported. Contact Support at https://www.npmjs.com/support for more info.
```

v5.0.2 is the latest published version; there is no upgrade path on npm.

Additionally, four transitive deprecation warnings come from Electron + electron-builder's own dependency tree (not Hermes's direct deps):

| Package | Source chain |
|---------|-------------|
| `inflight@1.0.6` | `electron` → `@electron/asar` → `glob@7` → `inflight` |
| `rimraf@2.6.3` | `electron-builder` → `electron-winstaller` → `temp` → `rimraf@2` |
| `glob@7.2.3` | Both chains above |
| `boolean@3.2.0` | `electron` → `@electron/get` → `global-agent` → `boolean` |

Upgrading `electron-builder` from `^26.8.1` to `^26.15.6` reduces but does not eliminate these — the remaining copies come from Electron itself (`@electron/asar`, `@electron/get`).

## Impact

- **Dev/build only** — `rcedit` is a `devDependency`, not shipped with the app.
- The script that uses it currently handles errors gracefully (after-pack.cjs swallows rejection), so a broken rcedit wouldn't block the build.
- Cosmetic nuisance on every `npm install` / `hermes update`.

## Possible fixes for rcedit

1. **Bundle the rcedit Rust binary directly** — the underlying tool lives at [electron/rcedit](https://github.com/electron/rcedit/releases) and still works. Download the Windows binary in a postinstall script instead of depending on the deprecated npm wrapper.
2. **Switch to `resedit`** (npm: `resedit`) — a pure-JS PE resource editor. Would need a rewrite of `set-exe-identity.cjs` since the API differs.
3. **Accept the warning** — the npm package still functions, just unsupported.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.17.0 (upstream efd87a15)
- Windows 10
- Node.js ≥20

﻿**Type:** Architecture / Cost Optimization
**Guideline Match:** "Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred. Anything that mutates past context... invalidates that cache and multiplies the user's cost."

**Description:**
The core agent loop currently risks injecting synthetic tool progress messages or modifying the system prompt based on dynamic context mid-conversation. Because providers like Anthropic and OpenAI require exact, byte-for-byte prefix matching to leverage prompt caching, any historical mutation destroys the cache for long-lived sessions, drastically inflating token costs and latency.

**Proposed Changes:**
- Introduce a strict ImmutablePrefixChain in un_agent.py to freeze the system prompt and historical turns.
- Refactor the conversation state manager to ensure any dynamic context (like changing environment details or synthetic alerts) is appended strictly as a trailing user-turn attachment for the current step, rather than mutating the prefix history.
- Add CI tests that assert the byte-stability of the first N-1 messages across conversational turns.

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Description
When the memory tool executor receives an invalid action (e.g. `action="list"` which is not a valid action — only `add`, `replace`, `remove` are valid), it produces this warning:

```
WARNING [session_id] agent.tool_executor: Tool memory returned error (0.00s): {"error": "Unknown action 'None'. Use: add, replace, remove", "success": false}
```

The error message says `"Unknown action None"` — but the actual action passed was not `"None"` (string). The agent tried to call `memory(action="list")` which is not a valid action. The string `"list"` gets converted to the Python literal `None` somewhere in the tool executor pipeline, then the error message reports that invalid `None` string.

## Expected behavior
- The error should show the actual invalid action string that was passed (e.g. `"list"`)
- Or the tool executor should validate the action parameter before passing it through, and fail with a clear validation error

## Steps to reproduce
1. Call `memory(action="list")` (which is not a valid action)
2. Observe the warning message showing `"Unknown action 'None'..."`

## Impact
- The error itself is harmless — the tool execution fails cleanly, memory operations in the same batch that have valid actions succeed
- The confusing error message may cause users to believe there is a deeper problem with the tool executor passing `None` as an action
- A batch of 3 memory operations that includes one invalid action will see the invalid one fail but the valid ones still succeed (atomic batch)

## Environment
- Hermes Agent version: 2.6.2
- Platform: macOS (Apple M2 Ultra, 128 GB RAM)
- Python: 3.11 / 3.12 (venv dual)

items.body:
## Product/feature

Hermes `com.hermes.browser-cdp` / browser CDP sidecar on macOS

## Environment

- macOS
- LaunchAgent: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.hermes.browser-cdp.plist`
- CDP port: `127.0.0.1:9222`
- Hermes browser profile: `~/.hermes/browser-cdp/chrome-profile`
- Observed Chrome version: `149.0.7827.201`
- Relevant sanitized env setting found: `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"`

## Bug summary

Hermes configured `com.hermes.browser-cdp` to launch the normal user-facing Google Chrome app bundle in headless mode:

```text
/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome --headless=new --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=~/.hermes/browser-cdp/chrome-profile ...
```

On macOS, this makes the system treat the invisible headless sidecar as “Google Chrome.” Dock/Finder/AppleScript activation then targets the headless process, so Chrome appears open but no visible windows appear, and creating a new Chrome window may fail or attach to the invisible headless instance.

## Observed behavior

- Chrome was shown as running/open.
- User could not see Chrome windows.
- `osascript`/Chrome reported browser windows, but WindowServer did not show them on-screen.
- `ps` showed the active Chrome app root was the Hermes headless process launched from `/Applications/Google Chrome.app`.
- Killing Chrome did not fix it because `com.hermes.browser-cdp` relaunched the headless Chrome.
- Normal Chrome became usable again only after the CDP sidecar stopped using the normal Chrome app identity.

## Expected behavior

Hermes browser-cdp should not use the normal user-facing `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` bundle as a long-lived headless LaunchAgent on macOS. It should use a separate browser identity/binary, such as:

- Playwright `chrome-headless-shell`
- Chrome for Testing
- Chromium
- another dedicated bundled/headless browser path

## Impact

This makes the user’s normal Chrome browser appear broken: Chrome is open but no windows are visible, and normal app activation/new-window behavior can fail. It is confusing and looks like a macOS/Chrome windowing problem, but the root cause is Hermes launching headless Chrome through the normal Chrome app bundle.

## Workaround applied locally

Changed only `ProgramArguments[0]` in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.hermes.browser-cdp.plist` from:

```text
/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome
```

to:

```text
~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1223/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell
```

After reloading the LaunchAgent:

- `com.hermes.browser-cdp` still ran.
- `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version` still responded.
- Normal Google Chrome opened visible windows again.

## Concern

This may return if Hermes update/reinstall/regeneration rewrites the LaunchAgent from `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` and that value still points to `/Applications/Google Chrome.app`.

## Request

Please update Hermes macOS browser-cdp setup so persistent headless CDP sidecars never use the normal Google Chrome.app bundle identity by default. Prefer `chrome-headless-shell`, Chrome for Testing, or a dedicated Chromium binary. Also consider detecting and warning when `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` points to `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` for a persistent headless LaunchAgent.

## Related issue

Related to #33155, but this report covers the current `com.hermes.browser-cdp` LaunchAgent path/profile/env setting and the verified `chrome-headless-shell` workaround.

items.title: Telegram: duplicate identical messages on short text-only turns (stream preview + gateway final send)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Upstream issue draft — Hermes Telegram duplicate on text-only turns

**Target:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/new  
**File locally:** `~/.hermes/UPSTREAM_ISSUE_TELEGRAM_DUPLICATE.md`  
**Status:** draft — not filed yet

---

## Title

```
Telegram: duplicate identical messages on short text-only turns (stream preview + gateway final send)
```

---

## Body (copy below this line)

### Summary

On Telegram with `streaming.enabled: true` and `transport: edit`, **short text-only turns** (single API call, no tools) often deliver the **same assistant text twice**: once via progressive stream edits, again via the gateway's normal `Sending response` path.

Multi-round tool turns usually suppress correctly (`Suppressing normal final send` in logs). The bug is specific to the **text-only + streaming** path.

### Environment

- Hermes gateway (`hermes gateway run`)
- Platform: Telegram DM
- Config (relevant excerpt):

```yaml
streaming:
  enabled: true
  transport: edit
  edit_interval: 0.8
display:
  platforms:
    telegram:
      streaming: true
      interim_assistant_messages: false
```

- Adapter: `REQUIRES_EDIT_FINALIZE: true` (Telegram MarkdownV2 finalize on last edit)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start gateway with Telegram streaming enabled (`transport: edit`).
2. Send a short greeting with no tool use expected, e.g. `hola` or `Hola Luna`.
3. Wait for single-turn completion (`api_calls=1` in gateway log).
4. Observe Telegram chat.

### Expected

One message with the assistant reply.

### Actual

Two **identical** messages (same text, same timestamp or consecutive).

### Log signature (broken turn)

Gateway log shows stream delivery **without** suppressing the final send:

```
INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=telegram ... api_calls=1 response=101 chars
INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Sending response (101 chars) to <chat_id>
```

**No** line like:

```
INFO gateway.run: Suppressing normal final send for session ... final delivery already confirmed
```

### Log signature (healthy tool turn — for contrast)

Multi-round turns often show suppress correctly:

```
INFO gateway.run: Suppressing normal final send for session agent:main:telegram:dm:<id>: final delivery already confirmed (streamed=True previewed=False content_delivered=True).
INFO gateway.run: response ready: ... api_calls=2 ...
```

(No second `Sending response` for the final body.)

### Diagnostic proof (isolate stream vs gateway)

Disable Telegram streaming only:

```yaml
display:
  platforms:
    telegram:
      streaming: false
```

Repeat step 2 → **duplicate disappears** (only gateway send path). Re-enable streaming → duplicate returns.

This confirms duplicate = **stream consumer delivered content + gateway sent again**, not a Telegram bot double-webhook issue.

### Root cause (hypothesis, partially confirmed)

In `gateway/run.py` (~line 15476), `response["already_sent"]` is set only when:

- `stream_consumer.final_response_sent`, or
- `final_content_delivered`, or
- `response_previewed`, or
- (after partial local fix) `streamed_body_matches(final)`

On short text-only turns, progressive edits show the **full** reply to the user, but `final_response_sent` / `content_delivered` often stay **False** at suppress-check time — likely because:

1. Final `finalize=True` edit (Telegram MarkdownV2) fails or is skipped after a successful progressive edit, **or**
2. `got_done` in `stream_consumer.py` does not mark delivery when `current_update_visible` is false but content was already shown, **or**
3. Race / `stream_task` timeout before flags are set (less common on ~15s turns).

Result: gateway falls through to `platforms/base.py` `Sending response` → duplicate.

### Proposed upstream fix

**Layer 1 — `gateway/stream_consumer.py` (`got_done`):**

When progressive edits already delivered the full accumulated text (`_last_sent_text` matches `_accumulated` modulo cursor), set `final_response_sent` and `final_content_delivered` even if the finalize-only edit fails (Telegram MDv2). Guard: do not do this after segment breaks that reset state mid tool-turn (see existing #25010 / #29346 semantics).

**Layer 2 — `gateway/run.py` (suppress check):**

Add safe fallback suppress for **text-only** turns:

```python
_text_only_stream_delivered = (
    api_calls == 1
    and stream_consumer.already_sent
    and stream_consumer.message_id
    and stream_consumer.message_id != "__no_edit__"
)
```

Include in suppress condition alongside existing `_streamed` / `_content_delivered` checks. The `api_calls == 1` guard prevents suppressing the real final answer when a stream only showed a **partial preamble** before tool rounds.

**Layer 3 — diagnostics:**

Log suppress-check state at INFO before decision:

```
Stream suppress check: already_sent, msg_id, final_response_sent, content_delivered,
body_match, visible_len, accum_len, final_len, api_calls
```

Helps distinguish finalize-failure vs race vs text mismatch without guessing.

### Verified fix (local patch, 2026-06-30)

Applied locally on `gateway/run.py` + `stream_consumer.py`. After patch, with streaming **re-enabled**:

```
INFO gateway.run: Stream suppress check session=...: already_sent=True msg_id=... final_response_sent=True content_delivered=True body_match=True visible_len=85 accum_len=85 final_len=85 api_calls=1
INFO gateway.run: Suppressing normal final send ... text_only_stream=True
```

User sees **one** Telegram message.

### Related code paths

- `gateway/run.py` — `_run_agent` finally block, suppress before return (~15463)
- `gateway/stream_consumer.py` — `got_done`, `_send_or_edit`, `REQUIRES_EDIT_FINALIZE`
- `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` — `edit_message(..., finalize=True)`

### Regression tests suggested

1. Mock Telegram adapter with `REQUIRES_EDIT_FINALIZE=True`: progressive edit succeeds, `got_done` finalize edit **fails**, accumulated == visible → must set `final_response_sent` (no gateway resend).
2. Tool turn with stream preamble + later final answer → must **not** suppress gateway send when `api_calls > 1`.
3. Integration: stream on, single text response → exactly one `adapter.send` for final body.

---

## File via GitHub CLI (optional)

From a machine with `gh` auth to NousResearch/hermes-agent:

```bash
gh issue create \
  --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent \
  --title "Telegram: duplicate identical messages on short text-only turns (stream preview + gateway final send)" \
  --body-file ~/.hermes/UPSTREAM_ISSUE_TELEGRAM_DUPLICATE.md
```

Or open the draft in an editor, copy the **Body** section only (without this header), and paste into the GitHub issue form.

---

## Local patch tracking

See `~/.hermes/LOCAL_PATCHES.md`. Re-apply after `hermes update` until upstream merges.

## Bug Description

In Desktop sidebar **project mode**, when a project has **no existing sessions**, clicking the worktree (fork) button creates a worktree successfully but the sidebar **shows nothing** — neither the "main" branch group nor the newly created worktree group appear. The list remains completely blank until the user starts a conversation, at which point the sidebar refreshes and both "main" and the worktree group become visible.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Desktop sidebar in **project mode**, enter a git repo workspace
2. Ensure the project has **zero sessions** (fresh project or all sessions archived/deleted)
3. Click the **fork button** (repo-forked icon) in the workspace group header to create a new worktree
4. Observe the sidebar

## Expected Behavior

After the worktree is created, the sidebar should immediately display:
- The "main" branch group (with no sessions under it)
- The newly created worktree group (with the new session under it)

## Actual Behavior

The sidebar shows **nothing** — the entire session list for this project is empty. The worktree is created on disk (confirmed via `git worktree list`), but the sidebar does not reflect it.

**Trigger for refresh:** Starting a new conversation in the project causes the sidebar to refresh, after which both "main" and the worktree group appear correctly.

## Suspected Root Cause

Same pattern as #54975 — the worktree creation path in `desktop-controller.tsx` does not call `refreshSessions()` after the `session.create` RPC (with `worktree: true`) completes. When the project already has sessions, the stale list still shows something (leading to the duplicate issue in #55725), but when the project has **zero** sessions, the stale list is empty and nothing renders at all until a full refresh is triggered by another event (e.g., sending a message).

## Related

- #39490 — feat(desktop): new session in a git worktree from the sidebar (the PR that introduced the fork button)
- #54975 — Desktop GUI: Sessions not refreshing when switching profile tabs (same root cause pattern: missing refresh trigger)
- #55725 — session duplicates under both new worktree group and main group after sidebar worktree creation (related symptom when sessions > 0)

items.title: Desktop secondary windows should support session switching or full-window mode

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Desktop currently has compact/secondary chat windows for opening a session or a fresh draft outside the main window. Those windows are helpful for visibility, but they are not full Desktop windows: they hide the main session sidebar/navigation and do not let the user switch the session inside that window.

This means the current secondary-window behavior does not fully solve the multi-window workflow. A user can open another OS window, but that window is effectively locked to one session/new-session draft and cannot be used like a normal Desktop window for browsing, resuming, or switching sessions.

## Current behavior

- The primary Desktop window has the normal sidebar/session list and can switch among sessions.
- A compact/secondary window can open a specific session or new-session draft.
- The secondary window is feature-limited and does not include the normal session switching/sidebar surface.
- To switch that secondary window to a different session, the user has to return to the main window and open a different auxiliary window instead of using the window they already have.

## Desired behavior

Support one of the following:

1. **Full main-window clone mode**
   - `File > New Window` / `Ctrl+Shift+N` can open a real full Desktop window with the same sidebar/navigation/session-switching capabilities as the primary window.
   - The new window can browse, resume, and switch sessions independently.

2. **Session switching inside secondary windows**
   - Keep compact session windows as a lightweight mode, but add a session picker/switcher inside them.
   - A secondary window can be retargeted from session A to session B without closing and reopening from the primary window.

Either approach would address the actual workflow need: multiple windows that can each move among sessions, not just single-session pop-outs.

## Why this matters

For users running multiple concurrent workstreams, windows are an acceptable alternative to tabs only if those windows are not locked to one session. A full clone of the main window would solve the same problem as tabbed sessions: keep multiple workspaces visible while still allowing normal session navigation within each window.

This is especially noticeable in the Windows Desktop client, where the current auxiliary window behavior feels like a limited pop-out rather than a second full Desktop surface.

## Related

- #40394 asks for multiple independent Desktop windows.
- #40499 is an open PR for opening sessions in multiple windows.
- #46951 added compact new-session windows, but those intentionally strip the sidebar/chrome and therefore do not cover this full-window/session-switching use case.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can open a second Desktop window and switch/resume sessions in that window without using the primary window.
- The UI clearly distinguishes compact single-session pop-outs from full Desktop windows if both modes continue to exist.
- Each window keeps its own active session/view state.
- Switching sessions in one window does not unexpectedly change the active session in another window.
- Works on Windows Desktop, not only macOS.

| 11:28:42 | Last successful Telegram inbound message received |
| 11:29:24 | Main turn completed, response delivered (587 chars, 42.7s) |
| 11:29:24 | bg-review thread spawned automatically (`Review the conversation above and consider saving to memory...`) |
| 11:29:24 | bg-review API call #1 fails: `APIConnectionError` to opencode-go (glm-5.2), streaming failed before delivery |
| 11:29:27 | bg-review retries, succeeds on attempt 2 |
| 11:30:12 | bg-review memory tool fails: `Operation 1 (remove): no entry matched 'NA'` |
| 11:30:23 | bg-review memory tool fails again: `After applying all 4 operations, memory would be at 1,494/1,375 chars -- over the limit` |
| 11:30:33 | bg-review finally completes (turn ended, agent closed) |
| 11:30:33 → 12:25 | **Telegram polling silently dead for ~55 minutes.** Process alive, zero log output, zero inbound messages. |

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04 (Linux, X11)
- **Python:** 3.11.15 (uv-managed)
- **Hermes:** v0.17.0 (2026.6.19)
- **Gateway:** systemd user service (`hermes-gateway.service`), linger enabled
- **Platform:** Telegram (bot token, polling mode)
- **Provider:** opencode-go (glm-5.2)
- **Network:** Verified stable — 0% packet loss to all endpoints, no WiFi disconnects

## What's NOT the cause

- ❌ Network instability (verified: 0% packet loss to opencode.ai, api.telegram.org, 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8)
- ❌ DNS failures (those were boot-time only, from systemd-resolved cache flush)
- ❌ Process crash (systemd showed active, process alive with 9 threads)
- ❌ Memory pressure (180MB working set)
- ❌ Telegram API outage (direct API calls work fine after restart)

## Suspected Root Cause

The bg-review thread's combination of (1) LLM connection error + retry and (2) repeated memory tool errors appears to stall or kill the Telegram polling coroutine/thread. The process doesn't crash — it just stops polling. This matches the pattern in #52942 (gateway silent crash, zero log output) and #47268 (bg-review shares session context, causing cascading failures).

The key difference from #52942: on Linux the process doesn't die (systemd doesn't restart it), it just goes brain-dead. On Windows it appears to crash outright. Either way, the result is the same: Telegram messages stop being received with no visible error.

## Related Issues

- #52942 — Gateway silent crash, zero log output (Windows, 15-19x/day)
- #47268 — BG Review shares session context with main loop, causing premature stop + memory error amplification
- #54118 — BG Review causes OOM with local llama.cpp server
- #52635 — Gateway silently drops all inbound messages (zero log output)

## Suggested Investigation

1. Does the bg-review thread share any resource (event loop, connection pool, session counter) with the Telegram polling loop that could cause a deadlock or stall?
2. Is there a watchdog/health-check for the Telegram polling thread itself? The process staying alive but not polling suggests the polling thread died but the main process didn't.
3. Could the memory tool errors in bg-review (exceeding char limit, failed remove operations) trigger an unhandled exception that kills the polling thread without logging?

## Workaround

`hermes gateway restart` recovers immediately. A watchdog cron that checks for stale gateway.log writes and auto-restarts would cap outage windows.

items.title: Multiplexed gateway: secondary profiles use default profile's credentials (all platforms)

labels.name: duplicate

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary

items.body:
## Bug Description

When `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` is set, the default gateway's multiplexer brings up adapters for every secondary profile. Each secondary profile's adapters are created inside `_profile_runtime_scope`, which installs a `secret_scope` contextvar so `get_secret()` resolves the profile's own credentials.

**However**, `load_gateway_config()` and platform adapter constructors (Matrix, Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost, and ~20 others) all read credentials via `os.getenv()` — not `get_secret()`. The `secret_scope` contextvar is invisible to `os.getenv()`, so every secondary profile's adapters are created with the **default profile's** credentials from the process-global `os.environ`.

## Impact

**All messaging platforms are affected**, not just Matrix. Any platform whose adapter or config loader reads tokens via `os.getenv()` (which is all of them — 158 callsites in `gateway/config.py` alone, plus dozens in adapter constructors) will use the default profile's credentials for every multiplexed profile.

Observed on a 9-profile Matrix deployment:
- Every profile's Matrix adapter connected as `@hermes:matrix.matthewpulsipher.net` (the default profile's user) instead of its own user ID
- Discord adapters for secondary profiles reported "No bot token configured" because `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` was read from the default's env (which has no Discord token)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create 2+ profiles, each with its own Matrix (or Discord/Telegram) credentials in their `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/.env`
2. Set `hermes config set gateway.multiplex_profiles true` (and the top-level `hermes config set multiplex_profiles true`)
3. Stop all secondary profile gateways, restart the default gateway
4. Check the gateway log: every profile connects with the default profile's token

```
grep "Matrix: using access token" ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log
```

All lines show the same user ID/device ID regardless of profile.

## Root Cause

`_profile_runtime_scope` (gateway/run.py) sets two contextvars:
1. `set_hermes_home_override` — redirects `get_hermes_home()` (contextvar, works)
2. `set_secret_scope` — installs profile secrets for `get_secret()` (contextvar, works)

But `load_gateway_config()` (gateway/config.py) resolves platform tokens via `os.getenv("MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN")`, `os.getenv("DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN")`, etc. — 158 `os.getenv` calls total. Platform adapter constructors have dozens more. None of these go through `get_secret()`.

The phase 2 commit (f538470cf4) migrated the **agent turn** path (runtime_provider, credential_pool, MCP config) to `get_secret()`, but the **platform adapter config** path was not migrated. The two paths use different credential resolution mechanisms, and only one honors the profile scope.

## Proposed Fix

Add an `overlay_environ` parameter to `_profile_runtime_scope`. When `True`, temporarily overlay the profile's `.env` onto `os.environ` so legacy `os.getenv()` callsites resolve the profile's credentials. When `False` (default), `os.environ` is untouched.

- Adapter creation callsites (startup, sequential): pass `overlay_environ=True`
- Per-turn agent path (concurrent): leave `False` to avoid racing on process-global `os.environ`

This is a minimal, backward-compatible fix. The default (`False`) preserves the existing per-turn behavior exactly. Migrating all 158 `os.getenv` callsites to `get_secret()` would be a larger follow-up.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (Mac Studio M1 Max)
- Python: 3.11.15 (Hermes venv)
- Hermes: latest main (f99ba56df4)
- 9 profiles, all on Matrix (each with unique user ID + access token on the same homeserver)

## Bug Description

When a provider is removed via the Desktop UI (Settings → Providers → API Keys → Remove), the provider continues to appear in the model picker dropdown with its full model list. The user sees all previously-authenticated providers as if they were never removed.

The bug spans two layers:

1. **Credential pool persistence** (`agent/credential_pool.py:_seed_from_env`): When the gateway starts, `_seed_from_env()` auto-creates `auth.json` credential pool entries with `source=env:{VAR}`. These entries persist indefinitely because `load_pool()` uses `prune_env_sources=False` — by design, to avoid cross-process races where one process's read deletes another's entry.

2. **Incomplete removal** (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:DELETE /api/env`): The Desktop "Remove" button calls `deleteEnvVar(key)` which removes the env var from `.env`, but never clears the corresponding credential pool entry from `auth.json`. The entry survives, and `list_authenticated_providers()` (`model_switch.py:1640-1644`) finds it via `read_credential_pool()` and marks the provider as authenticated.

Additionally, `read_credential_pool()` merges profile-scoped and global `auth.json` files — entries from one scope leak into the other's view.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop
2. Add an API key for a provider (e.g. DeepSeek) via Settings → Providers
3. Verify the provider appears in the model picker with models listed
4. Remove the API key via Settings → Providers → API Keys → Remove (trash icon)
5. Close and reopen the model picker
6. The provider still appears with its full model list

## Expected Behavior

Removing a provider's API key via Settings should remove the provider from the model picker on next open.

## Actual Behavior

The provider persists in the model picker with its full model list, even after the API key is removed. The only way to clear it is manually editing `~/.hermes/auth.json` to delete the credential pool entry.

## Affected Component

- Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)
- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (Desktop app)

## Debug Report

N/A — This is a credential pool persistence bug, not observable in gateway logs.

## Operating System

macOS 26.5.1

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

0.17.0

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

N/A

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_seed_from_env` in `agent/credential_pool.py` creates pool entries with `source=env:{VAR}` that persist after env var removal because `load_pool()` uses `prune_env_sources=False`. The Desktop's `DELETE /api/env` endpoint only removes the env var from `.env` via `remove_env_value()` — it never calls `write_credential_pool()` to clear the stale entry.

`read_credential_pool()` in `hermes_cli/auth.py:1208-1243` merges profile and global `auth.json` files, so entries from either scope show up in the model picker.

PR #55791 adds:
- `_clear_pool_entries_for_env_var()` to `hermes_cli/auth.py` — removes all env-seeded pool entries (`source=env:{VAR}`) and clears stale `suppressed_sources` flags

labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
### What happens

During a long (>30s) concurrent tool batch, the progress heartbeat status line (`concurrent tools running (Ns, K remaining: …)`) lists the wrong tool names when the batch also contains a guardrail-blocked / out-of-scope tool call.

### Where

`agent/tool_executor.py`, `execute_tool_calls_concurrent`:

```python
_still_running = [
    parsed_calls[futures.index(f)][1]
    for f in not_done
    if f in futures
]
```

`futures` is built in lock-step with `runnable_calls` (only the non-blocked calls), so `futures.index(f)` is a position in `runnable_calls` — but it indexes `parsed_calls`, which also includes the blocked calls. When a blocked call precedes a runnable one, the index shifts and the wrong tool name is reported.

### Reproduction

```python
# parsed_calls   = [blocked, runnable("read_file"), runnable("web_search")]
# runnable_calls = [(1, .., "read_file", {}), (2, .., "web_search", {})]
# futures        = [fA, fB]   # parallel to runnable_calls
# web_search (fB) still running:
[parsed_calls[futures.index(f)][1] for f in {fB} if f in futures]
# -> ["read_file"]   (should be ["web_search"])
```

### Impact

Cosmetic: only the names shown in the activity/heartbeat status are wrong. Tool execution, result-to-call mapping (which uses the original index), and ordering are unaffected.

### Expected

The heartbeat should index `runnable_calls` (which is parallel to `futures`) so the reported names match the actually-running tools.

A fix with regression tests is in #55808.

### Where

# chat()
return result["final_response"]

# main()
if result['final_response']:
    print(result['final_response'])

`run_conversation` (agent/conversation_loop.py) returns a result dict **without** `final_response` on its error paths (it includes `error` instead). ### Reproduction

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
from run_agent import AIAgent

agent = MagicMock()
agent.run_conversation.return_value = {
    "messages": [], "completed": False, "api_calls": 3,
    "error": "Request payload too large: max compression attempts (3) reached.",
    "partial": True, "failed": True, "compression_exhausted": True,
}
AIAgent.chat(agent, "hello")
# KeyError: 'final_response'
```

### Expected

`chat()` should return gracefully (e.g. an empty string) and `main()` should skip the final-response print, rather than raising `KeyError`, when the turn errored out.

items.title: Streaming fallback emits oversized Telegram messages for emoji text (_split_text_chunks treats UTF-16 limit as codepoints)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
### What happens

On the streaming-edit fallback path, an emoji-heavy final response can be split into chunks that exceed Telegram's length limit, so Telegram rejects the send ("Bad Request: message is too long") and the final response silently fails to deliver.

### Where

`gateway/stream_consumer.py`, `_split_text_chunks`:

```python
_cp_budget = _custom_unit_to_cp(remaining, limit, len_fn)
split_at = remaining.rfind("\n", 0, _cp_budget)
if split_at < limit // 2:     # limit is in the custom length unit
    split_at = limit          # but used as a codepoint slice index
chunks.append(remaining[:split_at])
```

`len_fn` is the adapter's length unit — Telegram passes `utf16_len` (UTF-16 code units). The no-newline fallback uses `limit` (UTF-16 units) as a codepoint index, so `remaining[:limit]` can be up to `2 * limit` UTF-16 units for astral characters (emoji are 2 units/codepoint).

### Reproduction

```python
def u16(s): return len(s.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2
from gateway.stream_consumer import GatewayStreamConsumer
chunks = GatewayStreamConsumer._split_text_chunks("😀" * 5000, 3996, len_fn=u16)
max(u16(c) for c in chunks)   # -> 7992 (limit was 3996)
```

Reached via `_send_fallback_final` (`safe_limit = MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH - 100 = 3996` on Telegram) when streaming edits fail and the response is emoji-heavy with no newline in the first half.

### Expected

Each chunk should fit within `limit` measured in the platform's own unit. Using the codepoint budget (`_custom_unit_to_cp`) for the fallback split and the half-limit check fixes it; default `len` behaviour is unchanged (budget == limit).

A fix with regression tests is in #55843.

items.title: Spawned subscription-authed CLIs (e.g. Claude Code) should get isolated, safe credential handling by default

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Summary
When hermes-agent spawns a subscription-authenticated CLI as a model/tool backend (concretely **Claude Code** on macOS), the framework does not isolate that child's credential context by default. The result is recurring, hard-to-diagnose **logouts of the user's interactive sessions**. We've patched it locally and would like the safe behavior to ship by default (happy to upstream the patch).

## Observed behavior
1. `LocalEnvironment` (`tools/environments/local.py`) strips provider secrets from child environments — correct for general API keys, but it also strips `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
2. A spawned `claude` (direct `claude -p …`, worker wrapper scripts, or the ACP path in `agent/copilot_acp_client.py`) therefore has **no subscription token** and falls through to the shared macOS Keychain / `~/.claude/.credentials.json` stores.
3. On auth failure, Claude Code **clears/nulls those shared credentials** — which logs out the user's *interactive* Claude sessions and the desktop app. The single-use OAuth refresh token rotating across two live stores compounds it.

## Impact
Silent, intermittent logouts that look like expiry or concurrency problems but aren't. Very hard to trace to the orchestrator. Affects anyone running Hermes with a subscription-authed Claude Code backend on macOS.

## Proposed default behavior
When the framework detects it's about to spawn a subscription-authed CLI:
- **Inject** the subscription token (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) into *only* that child env.
- **Strip** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` so stale/paid auth can't override the subscription token.
- **Isolate** the child with its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` so a failed/revoked agent token can never read or clobber the user's shared Keychain / `~/.claude` stores.
- **Fail before spawn** (with a clear log) if no token is available, instead of silently degrading into the shared store.

## Implementation

items.title: [Bug]: cron scheduler can raise "cannot schedule new futures" during gateway SIGTERM teardown

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the gateway receives SIGTERM (e.g. during `hermes update`, `hermes gateway stop`, or system shutdown), the cron scheduler can race the interpreter teardown and raise:

```
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
```

This happens because `cron/scheduler.py` has three code paths that call `executor.submit()` / `asyncio.run()` without checking whether the Python interpreter is already shutting down. During SIGTERM teardown, the background ticker thread and delivery path can still fire and attempt to schedule new futures.

## Affected paths (all in `cron/scheduler.py`)

1. **`_deliver_result()` standalone delivery path** (~L1471) — `asyncio.run(coro)` inside a `ThreadPoolExecutor` can hit interpreter shutdown mid-delivery.

2. **`_deliver_result()` RuntimeError fallback** (~L1478) — after `asyncio.run` fails, the recovery path creates a *new* `ThreadPoolExecutor` and calls `pool.submit()`, which also crashes if the interpreter is already shutting down.

3. **`_submit_with_guard()` in `tick()`** (~L2955) — `pool.submit(_run_and_release)` on every tick. If SIGTERM arrives mid-tick, this raises the RuntimeError.

## Reproduction

The error is intermittent (depends on SIGTERM timing), but reliably observed in `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` during:

```
hermes update    # restarts gateway internally
```

Example traceback in the log:

```
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
```

No user-visible breakage occurs (the process is dying anyway), but the traceback pollutes the error log on every gateway restart.

## Related issues

This is the same error pattern as #15073 and #15497 (Hindsight memory provider shutdown race), but in a **different subsystem** (`cron/scheduler.py` vs `plugins/memory/hindsight/`). Those issues are complementary, not duplicates — the cron scheduler has its own independent call paths that need the same guard.

Also related: #12175 (gateway failure shutdown skips cron ticker cleanup).

## Proposed fix

Add `sys.is_finalizing()` guards at the three affected paths. When the interpreter is shutting down, skip gracefully with a warning log instead of crashing:

```python
# 1. _deliver_result() standalone path (~L1471)
if sys.is_finalizing():
    logger.warning(
        "Job '%s': delivery skipped — interpreter is shutting down",
        job["id"],
    )
    delivery_errors.append("delivery skipped (interpreter shutdown)")
    continue

# 2. _deliver_result() RuntimeError fallback (~L1478)
if sys.is_finalizing():
    logger.warning(
        "Job '%s': delivery skipped — interpreter shutdown during standalone fallback",
        job["id"],
    )
    delivery_errors.append("delivery skipped (interpreter shutdown)")
    continue

# 3. _submit_with_guard() in tick() (~L2955)
if sys.is_finalizing():
    logger.warning(
        "Job '%s': submission skipped — interpreter is shutting down",
        job.get("name", job_id),
    )
    with _running_lock:
        _running_job_ids.discard(job_id)
    return None
```

`sys` is already imported at module level (`import sys` at L21), so no new imports needed.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0
- macOS (also reproduced on Linux)

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — I have the patch ready and can submit a PR.

items.body:
## Summary

PR #55921 makes the Telegram gateway **self-heal** when its PTB `Updater` stops while the process stays alive (#55769). That's the right defensive layer — the gateway now recovers regardless of what killed the poller. But it treats the symptom, not the trigger. This issue tracks investigating *why* a background-review thread's failures can take down the polling coroutine in the first place.

## Observed trigger (from #55769)

The reporter's timeline shows polling goes dead immediately after a bg-review thread hits:

1. An `APIConnectionError` to the LLM provider (streaming failed before delivery), then a retry that succeeds.
2. Two memory-tool failures in a row (`no entry matched 'NA'`, then `memory would be at 1,494/1,375 chars -- over the limit`).

After the bg-review turn ends, the Telegram long-poll task is simply gone (`updater.running == False`) — process alive, send path healthy, no logged exception.

## Questions to answer

1. Does the bg-review fork share any resource with the Telegram polling loop — event loop, httpx connection pool, session counter, a cancellation scope — that a failure path could tear down or cancel?
2. Can an unhandled exception (or an over-broad `cancel()`/cleanup) in the bg-review thread propagate to or cancel the polling task without surfacing in logs?
3. Why is there zero log output when the poller dies? A swallowed `CancelledError` or a bare `except` in the bg-review teardown is the likely culprit.

## Related

- #55769 — the bug report (symptom)
- #55921 — the self-heal fix (this issue is the trigger follow-up)
- #47268 — bg-review shares session context with main loop, causing premature stop + memory-error amplification
- #54118 — bg-review OOM with local llama.cpp
- #52942 — gateway silent crash, zero log output (Windows variant)

## Scope

Code analysis only — do not assume the reporter's setup. Trace the bg-review fork lifecycle in `run_agent.py` (`_spawn_background_review`) against the gateway's polling task ownership in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`, looking for shared/cancellable state.

items.title: TUI/Desktop ignores disabled streaming and crashes MoA Codex aggregator with SimpleNamespace not iterable

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

In the Desktop/TUI runtime, Hermes still takes the provider streaming path even when streaming is disabled in config. This breaks profiles using a Mixture of Agents (MoA) model whose aggregator is `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5`.

The failure shown to the user is:

```text
Error: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object is not iterable
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `v0.17.0 (2026.6.19)` / upstream `d8083221`
- OS: macOS ARM64
- Runtime surface affected: Desktop/TUI (`platform=tui`)
- Plain CLI behavior: works once `display.streaming: false` is set
- Model config involved:

```yaml
model:
  provider: moa
  base_url: moa://local
  default: default

moa:
  presets:
    default:
      aggregator:
        provider: openai-codex
        model: gpt-5.5
```

The affected profile also had streaming disabled:

```yaml
display:
  streaming: false

streaming:
  enabled: false
  transport: auto
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a profile to use MoA as the active model.
2. Configure the MoA aggregator slot to use `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5`.
3. Disable streaming in config:

   ```bash
   hermes -p <profile> config set display.streaming false
   ```

   and ensure top-level gateway streaming is disabled as well:

   ```yaml
   streaming:
     enabled: false
   ```

4. Start the profile in Desktop/TUI, e.g.:

   ```bash
   hermes -p <profile> chat --tui
   ```

5. Send any prompt, e.g. `ping`.

## Expected Behavior

When streaming is disabled, Desktop/TUI should avoid provider token streaming and run the non-streaming request path. The MoA Codex aggregator should return a normal completed response and the UI should display it.

## Actual Behavior

The Desktop/TUI run still fails with:

```text
Error: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object is not iterable
```

Logs show the failing path is TUI-specific:

```text
agent.turn_context: conversation turn: ... provider=moa platform=tui ...
agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object is not iterable
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed ... provider=moa base_url=moa://local model=default summary='types.SimpleNamespace' object is not iterable
```

The same profile works from plain CLI after disabling `display.streaming`:

```bash
assetwise chat -q "ping" --verbose
```

returns:

```text
pong
```

## Investigation / Likely Cause

`display.streaming: false` is honored by the plain CLI path (`cli.py` reads it into `streaming_enabled`).

However, the TUI gateway appears to pass `stream_callback` to `run_conversation()` unconditionally in `tui_gateway/server.py`:

```python
run_kwargs = {
    "conversation_history": list(history),
    "stream_callback": _stream,
}
result = agent.run_conversation(run_message, **run_kwargs)
```

That makes the agent use the streaming path even when config disables streaming.

With MoA + `openai-codex` aggregator, the streaming path expects an iterable stream of chat-completion chunks. The Codex auxiliary adapter consumes the Codex Responses stream internally and returns a completed `types.SimpleNamespace` response object instead. The streaming loop then attempts to iterate it, producing:

```text
'types.SimpleNamespace' object is not iterable
```

## Suggested Fix

Either/both of:

1. TUI/Desktop should respect streaming config before passing `stream_callback` into `run_conversation()`.
2. MoA + Codex aggregator streaming should not return a completed `SimpleNamespace` where the caller expects a raw iterable stream; either return a real stream or force non-streaming for this adapter path.

## Workarounds

- Use plain CLI with `display.streaming: false`.
- Avoid MoA as the active model in Desktop/TUI when the aggregator is `openai-codex`.
- Use a non-Codex aggregator for MoA until the TUI streaming/config path is fixed.

items.title: Windows: ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler lock contention freezes gateway after some time (Cannot acquire lock after 20 attempts)

labels.name: comp/cli

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows, the Hermes gateway freezes after some time because `concurrent_log_handler`'s `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler` gets stuck on file lock contention. Multiple processes (Desktop app, gateway, dashboard) all try to write to the same rotating log files (`gateway.log`, `agent.log`). Each process creates its own `.__<name>.lock` file via `portalocker`. When a process crashes or is killed uncleanly, its lock file remains stale — other processes cannot acquire the lock, and after 20 attempts they raise:

```
RuntimeError: Cannot acquire lock after 20 attempts
```

This blocks the asyncio event loop of the gateway because every logging call is a blocking lock operation. The gateway stops processing messages, and the Desktop app shows "request prompt submit" errors because the backend is unresponsive.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Hermes version:** v0.17.0 (also reproduced on v0.16.0)
- **Surface:** Desktop app (Electron) + CLI + gateway

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes Desktop (or `hermes gateway run`)
2. Let it run for a while with multiple profiles/backends active
3. After some time (minutes to hours), the backend becomes unresponsive
4. Desktop shows "request prompt submit" — cannot connect to backend

## Actual Behavior

- `gateway-stdio.log` fills with hundreds of `RuntimeError: Cannot acquire lock after 20 attempts`
- `gateway.log` stops updating
- The gateway asyncio loop freezes on the blocking lock attempt
- Manual restart (`hermes gateway stop && rm -f .__*.lock && hermes gateway start`) temporarily fixes it

## Expected Behavior

The logging system should never deadlock the gateway. Lock contention in the logging subsystem should not bring down the entire agent.

## Root Cause

`hermes_logging.py` (lines 60-63) imports `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler` on Windows:

```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    from concurrent_log_handler import (
        ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler as RotatingFileHandler,
    )
```

This handler uses `portalocker` for cross-process file locking. On Windows, this creates lock files (`.__<name>.lock`) that persist after process death. The lock acquisition is blocking and has no timeout beyond the 20-attempt limit — when it fails, the exception propagates through the logging stack and freezes the asyncio dispatcher.

## Suggested Fix

Replace `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler` with stdlib `logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler` on Windows, with a graceful fallback in `doRollover()` that catches `PermissionError` (WinError 32 — happens when another process holds an open handle during rollover) and skips rotation instead of crashing:

1. Remove the Windows-specific `concurrent_log_handler` import — always use stdlib `RotatingFileHandler`
2. Remove `_CONCURRENT_LOG_LOCK_TIMEOUT` and `_is_windows_concurrent_log_lock_timeout()` helper (no longer needed)
3. Remove the `handleError` override (stdlib does not raise lock timeout)
4. Wrap `doRollover()` in `_ManagedRotatingFileHandler` with `try/except PermissionError` so rotation is gracefully skipped when another process holds the file

This eliminates all lock files (`.__*.lock`), removes the deadlock vector entirely, and handles the WinError 32 rename problem by simply skipping rotation when the file is busy — logging continues uninterrupted.

## Related Issues

- #48316 — Hermes CLI cannot find concurrent_log_handler (opposite problem — missing dependency)
- #54622 — Stale lock/WAL files after unclean shutdown prevent restart (same root cause — lock files from concurrent_log_handler)

## Workaround

```bash
hermes gateway stop
rm -f "$HOME/AppData/Local/hermes/logs/.__*.lock"
hermes gateway start
```

items.body:
### Bug Description


Hermes Desktop (Electron) has a race condition in the backend lifecycle. When BootFailureOverlay triggers a Repair, the hermes:bootstrap:repair IPC handler kills the backend process with SIGTERM but does not wait for it to exit before returning. The renderer immediately calls window.location.reload(), which spawns a new backend via startHermes() — but the old backend may still hold the port. Port conflict → new backend fails → overlay appears again → user clicks Repair → repeat → 🔄 SIGTERM crash loop.

Steps to Reproduce

Run Hermes Desktop
Let the backend fail (e.g., kill the Python process externally, or let a timeout occur)
BootFailureOverlay appears
Click "Repair" button
repairBootstrap kills backend via resetHermesConnection() and returns immediately
Renderer calls window.location.reload() → startHermes() spawns a new backend
New backend fails because old backend's port is not yet released
Overlay appears again → Go to step 4
Affected Component
Desktop / Electron — apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs

Root Cause

resetHermesConnection() (~L12927) kills the process without waiting:

function resetHermesConnection() {
  connectionPromise = null;
  backendStartFailure = null;
  if (hermesProcess && !hermesProcess.killed) {
    hermesProcess.kill("SIGTERM");   // ← no await, no waitForExit
  }
  hermesProcess = null;
  resetBootProgressForReconnect();
}
hermes:bootstrap:repair handler (~L13769) calls it without awaiting exit:

ipcMain.handle("hermes:bootstrap:repair", async () => {
  // ...clear marker...
  bootstrapFailure = null;
  backendStartFailure = null;
  resetHermesConnection();            // ← called but not awaited on exit
  return { ok: true };
});

Notably, the sibling hermes:bootstrap:reset handler (~L13752) does it correctly — it uses teardownPrimaryBackendAndWait() which waits for the process to actually exit (with a 5s timeout + force-kill fallback). repair should follow the same pattern.

Proposed Fix

Replace resetHermesConnection() in the hermes:bootstrap:repair handler with await teardownPrimaryBackendAndWait() — identical to what reset handler already does. This ensures the old backend has released its port before the new one is spawned.

-  resetHermesConnection();
+  await teardownPrimaryBackendAndWait();

We've verified this fix locally:
✅ node --check main.cjs passes
✅ 129/131 Electron platform tests pass (1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change)

### Actual Behavior

The "Repair" action sends SIGTERM to the old backend but returns immediately without

## Bug Description

Clicking the **Log Out** button in the Hermes dashboard causes an unhandled `NotImplementedError` in the `BasicAuthProvider`, which crashes the dashboard ASGI application. The gateway then shuts down cleanly (exit code 0) and the container enters a restart loop when `restart: unless-stopped` is set in docker-compose.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the container with `restart: unless-stopped` (or any restart policy)
2. Log in to the dashboard successfully
3. Click the **Log Out** button in the dashboard UI
4. Observe: the dashboard returns a 500 error and the container restarts

## Expected Behavior

Logging out should terminate the session cleanly and redirect to the login page without crashing the server.

## Actual Behavior

```
File "/opt/hermes/plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py", line 230, in start_login
    raise NotImplementedError(
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow.
The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

The error originates in `auth_login` route (`dashboard_auth/routes.py:197`) which calls `p.start_login(redirect_uri=...)`. For `BasicAuthProvider`, this method is not implemented because it is password-only. This causes an unhandled exception to propagate through the ASGI middleware stack, ultimately crashing the dashboard server.

The gateway then receives SIGTERM and shuts down:
```
WARNING gateway.run: Shutdown context: signal=SIGTERM under_systemd=no parent_pid=139 parent_name=s6-supervise
hermes-agent-1 exited with code 0 (restarting)
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: v0.17.0 (2026.6.19), upstream d8083221
- Deployment: Docker container with nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
- Dashboard auth provider: basic (password-only)
- docker-compose restart policy: unless-stopped

## Root Cause

In `plugins/dashboard_auth/routes.py`, the `auth_login` route unconditionally calls `p.start_login(redirect_uri=...)` without checking whether the auth provider supports OAuth redirects:

```python
# dashboard_auth/routes.py:197
ls = p.start_login(redirect_uri=_redirect_uri(request))
```

The `BasicAuthProvider.start_login()` raises `NotImplementedError` because it has no OAuth flow - it only supports password POST to `/auth/password-login`.

## Suggested Fix

In `dashboard_auth/routes.py`, add a check before calling `start_login`:

```python
if hasattr(p, 'start_login') and callable(getattr(p, 'start_login', None)):
    ls = p.start_login(redirect_uri=_redirect_uri(request))
else:
    # Provider doesn't support OAuth redirect - fall through to password login
    ...
```

Or alternatively, check if the provider is `BasicAuthProvider` and skip the OAuth redirect call.

## Workaround

Do not use the dashboard logout button. Instead, restart the container cleanly:

```bash
docker compose restart
# or
docker compose down && docker compose up -d
```

items.body:
Title: Telegram polling silently dies after network error + self-restart

## What happened

Been running Hermes on two machines (Win10 desktop + Linux Docker) and both hit the same thing: after a network blip, Telegram goes silent but everything looks healthy.

## How to reproduce

1. Gateway happily polling Telegram
2. Network hiccup — `httpx.ConnectError` a few times
3. After 10 consecutive failures, adapter does its thing: "Fatal telegram adapter error → Restarting gateway"
4. Reconnect happens, log says `✓ telegram connected`
5. ...and that's it. Gateway never processes another message. Log goes completely dead. But the process is still there, still responds to SIGTERM, state file still says "running" and "connected".

## What I found digging into it

**Docker instance (29+ hour outage):**
- Between "reconnected" and the next log line: **6 hours 9 minutes of absolutely nothing**
- After a container restart, it happened again within 3.5 hours — so it's not an uptime accumulation thing
- State file `updated_at` timestamp froze at the moment of reconnect, never updated again
- Process PID stayed the same across 4 `gateway.start` events with zero `gateway.exit` events between them — same process reinitializing itself
- During one reconnect attempt got: `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'updater'`

**Windows instance:**
- Process actually died (exit code 267009) rather than lingering
- State file stuck at "starting"

## My guess at the bug

When the adapter does its self-restart dance:
1. Old polling task gets cancelled
2. New Telegram connection establishes fine
3. "connected" flag gets flipped on
4. But the new polling task either never starts, or starts and immediately exits silently

The `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'updater'` during reconnect makes me think the adapter object is in a half-destroyed, half-recreated state.

## Why this is nasty

State-file-based monitoring thinks everything is fine. `gateway_state.json` says "running" + "connected". PID is alive. The only way I caught it was noticing the log had been dead for hours.

## Current workaround

External cron script that checks if `gateway_state.json` `updated_at` timestamp is > 2 hours old → restart. Works but obviously not ideal.

Happy to provide full logs if that helps.

items.title: Bug: execute_code sandbox ignores the per-session cwd override, diverges from write_file/terminal

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

`execute_code`'s sandbox subprocess does **not** resolve its cwd against the per-session cwd override registered by `session.cwd.set`, even though the sibling file tools (`write_file`/`read_file`/`patch`) and `terminal` do. So in a multi-session gateway where each session pins its own workspace via `session.cwd.set`, code run through `execute_code` writes to the **process launch directory** (shared across sessions) while `write_file` in the same turn writes to the **session workspace** — the two file-writing paths in one session silently disagree on the working directory.

## Reproduce

Gateway/dashboard with two sessions on the same process, each having called:

```jsonc
// session A
session.cwd.set({session_id: "aaa", cwd: "/work/session-a"})
// session B
session.cwd.set({session_id: "bbb", cwd: "/work/session-b"})
```

In session A, prompt the agent to:

1. `write_file("flag.txt", "A")`  → lands in `/work/session-a/flag.txt` ✅
2. `execute_code('open("flag.txt","w").write("A")')`  → lands in **`<process launch dir>/flag.txt`** ❌ (not `/work/session-a/`)

Both writes happen in the same session, same turn, yet the file ends up in different directories.

## Root cause

`session.cwd.set` registers the workspace through `register_task_env_overrides(session_key, {"cwd": ...})` (terminal_tool), keyed by the raw session/task id. `prompt.submit` forwards that id as `task_id` into `run_conversation` and on into `execute_code(task_id=...)` (`tui_gateway/server.py` ~L7253).

The override is honored by:
- `write_file`/`read_file`/`patch` → `tools/file_tools.py::_resolve_base_dir` → `_registered_task_cwd_override(task_id)` ✅
- `terminal` → `_resolve_command_cwd` uses `env.cwd`, which `register_task_env_overrides` syncs (terminal_tool ~L979-990) ✅

But **not** by `execute_code`:

```python
# tools/code_execution_tool.py  (v0.17.0, commit 7fb2027d)
def _resolve_child_cwd(mode: str, staging_dir: str) -> str:   # ← no task_id
    if mode != "project":
        return staging_dir
    raw = os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD", "").strip()           # ← process-wide env only
    if raw: ...
    here = os.getcwd()                                          # ← process launch dir
    ...
```

`_resolve_child_cwd` (1) is never passed `task_id`, and (2) only consults `$TERMINAL_CWD` (a process-global) and `os.getcwd()` — it never calls `_registered_task_cwd_override(task_id)` / `resolve_task_overrides(task_id)`. The task_id that would key the lookup is available at the call site (`execute_code`'s `task_id` arg) but dropped.

Docstring intent ("project: the session's working directory") confirms this is unintended: the session cwd is reachable, the function just doesn't read it.

## Impact

Medium. No crash, no error — but **silent data misplacement**: across N sessions on one process, every `execute_code` write lands in the same launch dir, overwriting each other, while `write_file` correctly partitions by session. Skills that mix `execute_code` and `write_file` see inconsistent file locations. Easy to misattribute to the skill or the frontend.

## Suggested fix

Pass `task_id` through and query the override first (mirrors `write_file`/`terminal`):

```python
def _resolve_child_cwd(mode: str, staging_dir: str, task_id: str = "") -> str:
    if mode != "project":
        return staging_dir
    # 1. per-session cwd override (session.cwd.set), like write_file
    if task_id:
        try:
            from tools.file_tools import _registered_task_cwd_override
            sess_cwd = _registered_task_cwd_override(task_id)
            if sess_cwd and os.path.isdir(sess_cwd):
                return sess_cwd
        except Exception:
            pass
    # 2/3/4. TERMINAL_CWD / getcwd / staging  (unchanged)
    raw = os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD", "").strip()
    ...
```

and at the single call site (~L1283):

```python
_child_cwd = _resolve_child_cwd(_mode, tmpdir, task_id=task_id or "")
```

Back-compat verified: with `task_id` empty or no override registered, behavior is identical to today; `strict` mode is unchanged.

## Environment

- hermes-agent `0.17.0` (commit `7fb2027d`)
- gateway/dashboard (TUI gateway), local terminal backend, project execution mode

items.body:
## Summary

When the iteration budget is exhausted, `handle_max_iterations` (chat_completion_helpers.py:1411) appends a synthetic user message to `messages` at line 1420:

```python
messages.append({"role": "user", "content": summary_request})
```

Then makes an API call to get a summary. **If the API call fails** (network error, auth error, provider outage), the except block at line 1634 catches the exception and sets `final_response` to an error string — but does NOT append it to `messages`.

The synthetic user message is left orphaned in the conversation history without a corresponding assistant response. On session resume, the model sees two consecutive user messages, violating the role alternation invariant. Strict providers (Gemini, Claude) reject this.

## Impact

- Session is permanently corrupted with a role alternation violation
- Happens specifically when the model/provider is already failing (the worst time to corrupt state)
- Strict providers reject the session on resume
- The synthetic message ("You've reached the maximum number of tool-calling iterations...") appears as a real user message to the model

## Reproduction

1. Configure a model/provider that will fail after N retries
2. Send a message that triggers N+1 tool calls
3. The iteration budget is exhausted, `_handle_max_iterations` is called
4. The summary API call also fails (same provider issue)
5. The exception propagates; the session is persisted
6. Resume the session — the model sees two consecutive user messages

## Fix

Append the error response as an assistant message in the except block, matching the success path behavior.

# Bug: Desktop chat model picker persists to global config instead of session-scoped override

## Summary
When switching models using the **status bar / chat model picker** in Hermes Desktop on Windows, the change persists to the global `~/.hermes/config.yaml` instead of applying only to the current session. This contradicts the documented behavior where chat picker should be session-scoped and global defaults should only be changed via **Settings → Model**.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open an existing chat session in Hermes Desktop on Windows
2. Verify current global model in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (e.g., `model.default = gpt-5.4`)
3. Switch model using the **status bar / chat model picker** (select a different model like `glm-4.7`)
4. Verify `~/.hermes/config.yaml` has been modified (check mtime, hash, size)
5. Observe that `model.default` has changed globally to the newly selected model

## Expected Behavior
Model switch from chat picker should:
- Apply **per-session only** (session-scoped override)
- **NOT** modify `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
- Keep global default unchanged
- Global default should only be modified via **Settings → Model**

## Actual Behavior
Chat model picker modifies `~/.hermes/config.yaml` and changes the global default to the newly selected model.

## Environment
- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Hermes Version:** Latest (active session as of 2026-07-01)
- **Session:** Desktop TUI

## Evidence / Testing Results

### Test 1: Chat model picker (bug behavior)
- **Before:** `model.default = gpt-5.4`, `provider = openai-codex`
- **After picker switch:** `model.default = glm-4.7`, `provider = zai`
- **Config file:** Modified (mtime changed, hash changed, size changed from 14766 to 14753 bytes)
- **Status:** ❌ Global config was modified

### Test 2: Slash command `--session` (correct behavior)
- **Before:** `model.default = glm-4.7`, `provider = zai`
- **After `/model gpt-5.4 --session`:** `model.default = glm-4.7` (unchanged)
- **Config file:** Unmodified (mtime, hash, size unchanged)
- **Status:** ✅ Global config remained unchanged, session model switched correctly

## Workaround
Use slash command with `--session` flag for per-session model switches:
```bash
/model <model_name> --session
/model gpt-5.4 --session
/model glm-5.2 --provider zai --session
```

Or set the desired global default once via **Settings → Model**, then use per-session switches only when needed.

## Impact
- Users expecting per-session model switches (as documented in comments) end up changing their global defaults unintentionally
- Frequent model switching via chat picker leads to unintended global config pollution
- Confusion between "session-scoped" picker and "global" settings

## Suggested Fix
Add session-scoped behavior to chat model picker:

1. **When active session exists:**
   - Send `config.set` with session model override (not global)
   - Do NOT write to `config.yaml`

2. **Add UI toggle for model picker:**
   - "Apply to this session only" (default for chat picker)
   - "Apply as new default" (redirect to Settings → Model behavior)

3. **Respect `model.persist_switch_by_default` flag:**
   - Read from `config.yaml`
   - Desktop UI should honor this flag (currently it seems to ignore it)

- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts` - `selectModel` function
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-menu-panel.tsx` - Model picker UI
- `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` - `setModelAssignment` API call
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py` - `POST /api/model/set` endpoint (writes to config.yaml)

## Summary

MCP tool results are returned as raw strings with **zero size enforcement**. The result is collected from MCP content blocks, joined, and returned directly into the agent's tool-result pipeline — with no truncation, no byte cap, and no token estimate check.

Contrast this with:
- **Terminal tool**: truncates output at `get_max_bytes()` (default 50KB)

- This floods the conversation context window, triggering context overflow
- On memory-constrained deployments, can cause OOM
- Token costs are unbounded

## Fix

Apply the same `get_max_bytes()` truncation used by the terminal tool.

items.title: [Bug]: ESC interrupt + queued message send causes user message bubble to vanish
items.body:
## Bug Description

When the model is generating and the user has a queued message, pressing ESC interrupts the current turn and auto-drains the queued message. The message is successfully sent to the gateway and the model responds normally, but the **user message bubble disappears** from the conversation history. The user sees the model responding to a message that isn't visible.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a conversation, send a message that triggers a long generation
2. While the model is generating, type another message → it gets queued
3. Press ESC to interrupt the current turn
4. Observe the conversation

## Expected Behavior

The queued message should appear as a user message bubble, followed by the model's response.

## Actual Behavior

- ✅ The queued message IS sent to the gateway (model responds normally)
- ❌ The user message bubble vanishes from the conversation transcript
- The user sees the model responding to an invisible message

## Root Cause

Race condition between `hydrateFromStoredSession` and the queue auto-drain in `desktop-controller.tsx`:

1. `cancelRun` sets `interrupted=true`, `busy=false`
2. `completeAssistantMessage` bails early (interrupted), but `shouldHydrate` was already computed as `true` (no user tail at evaluation time)
3. `hydrateFromStoredSession(3, ...)` starts an async fetch (up to 3 retries × 250ms delay)
4. Auto-drain fires → `submitPromptText` → optimistic user message added to session state
5. Hydration fetch resolves → `preserveLocalAssistantErrors(backendMessages, state.messages)` **replaces** the entire messages array with the backend snapshot, which hasn't persisted the queued message yet → bubble vanishes

The key is that `shouldHydrate` is evaluated synchronously in `completeAssistantMessage` BEFORE the auto-drain adds the optimistic message. The hydration fetch then runs asynchronously and its updater overwrites the state.

## Affected Files

- `apps/desktop/src/app/desktop-controller.tsx` — `hydrateFromStoredSession`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/index.ts` — `completeAssistantMessage` (where `shouldHydrate` is computed)

items.body:
## Bug

The dashboard auth middleware auto-redirects unauthenticated users to `/auth/login?provider=<name>` when there is exactly one session provider registered. When that provider is password-only (e.g. `BasicAuthProvider` with `supports_password=True`), `/auth/login` calls `start_login()` which raises `NotImplementedError` → **500 Internal Server Error**.

## Reproduction

1. Configure the dashboard with only a basic auth provider (username/password) — e.g. `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` / `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` / `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET` in `.env`.
2. Bind with `--host 0.0.0.0 --insecure` (so `auth_required=True`).
3. Visit `http://<host>:9119/` in a browser.
4. Observe 500 Internal Server Error.

## Root Cause

In `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py`, `_auto_sso_response()` (line ~187-191):

```python
provider = providers[0]
prefix = prefix_from_request(request)
next_param = _safe_next_target(request)
from urllib.parse import quote
auth_login = f"{prefix}/auth/login?provider={quote(provider.name, safe='')}"
if next_param:
    auth_login = f"{auth_login}&next={next_param}"
resp = RedirectResponse(url=auth_login, status_code=302)
```

This unconditionally redirects to `/auth/login` — the OAuth redirect endpoint — regardless of whether the provider supports OAuth. `BasicAuthProvider.start_login()` raises:

```
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

The `/auth/login` route (`routes.py` line 190) checks `supports_session` (which defaults to `True` on `BasicAuthProvider` since it inherits from the base class) but does NOT check `supports_password` before calling `start_login()`.

## Expected Behavior

When the single session provider has `supports_password=True` (and no OAuth capability), the middleware should redirect to `/login` (the credential form page) instead of `/auth/login` (the OAuth redirect endpoint). The `/login` page correctly renders a username/password form that POSTs to `/auth/password-login`.

## Fix

In `_auto_sso_response()`, check `supports_password` before choosing the redirect target:

```python
if getattr(provider, "supports_password", False):
    login_url = f"{prefix}/login"
    if next_param:
        login_url = f"{login_url}?next={next_param}"
else:
    login_url = f"{prefix}/auth/login?provider={quote(provider.name, safe='')}"
    if next_param:
        login_url = f"{login_url}&next={next_param}"

resp = RedirectResponse(url=login_url, status_code=302)
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent 0.17.0 (release 2026.6.19)
- Config: `platform_toolsets` with basic auth provider only
- Dashboard launched with `--host 0.0.0.0 --insecure --no-open --tui`
- Python 3.11

## Workaround

Manually navigate to `/login` instead of `/` — the password form loads correctly and login works. The 500 only occurs on the auto-redirect from root.
