## Dashboard returns HTTP 500 on non-loopback bind with basic auth

### Summary

When the Hermes web dashboard is bound to a non-loopback interface (e.g. a
Tailscale IP / hostname) with `basic_auth` configured, hitting `/` returns
HTTP 500 with `NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only`
inside `start_login()`. The login form is unreachable.

### Reproduction

1. Configure basic auth in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   dashboard:
     basic_auth:
       username: admin
       password_hash: scrypt$16384$8$1$<salt>$<hash>
       password: ''
       secret: ''
       session_ttl_seconds: 0
   ```
2. Start the dashboard bound to a non-loopback interface:
   ```
   hermes dashboard --host <tailscale-ip-or-hostname> --port 9119 --no-open
   ```
3. Visit `http://<host>:<port>/` in a browser.

### Expected

- `GET /` (unauthenticated) → `302 Found` → `Location: /login?next=%2F`
- `GET /login` → `200 OK` with the password form
- Login completes and redirects back to the original path

### Actual

- `GET /` → `302 Found` → `Location: /auth/login?provider=basic&next=%2F`
- Browser follows to `/auth/login?provider=basic`
- Server returns `500 Internal Server Error`
- In `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` (or systemd journal for the dashboard unit):
  ```
  NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no
  OAuth redirect flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
    File ".../hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py", line 197, in auth_login
      ls = p.start_login(redirect_uri=_redirect_uri(request))
    File ".../plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py", line 230, in start_login
      raise NotImplementedError(...)
  ```

### Root cause

In `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py::_auto_sso_response()`, the
middleware treats a single registered session provider as a valid OAuth
redirect target and sends browsers to `/auth/login?provider=<name>`. For
`BasicAuthProvider` that route crashes inside `start_login()` because the
provider is password-only.

`list_session_providers()` filters on `supports_session=True`, and the
base class `DashboardAuthProvider` defaults `supports_session = True`
(`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/base.py:179`). `BasicAuthProvider` inherits
that default and never overrides it, so the auto-redirect middleware
treats it as a valid OAuth provider.

The login page itself handles this correctly — `_render_providers()`
(`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/login_page.py:484-487`) renders a password
form for `supports_password=True` providers instead of an OAuth button.
The bug is that the auto-redirect middleware uses a different (and
incompatible) signal than the login page uses.

### Suggested fix

Add a guard in `_auto_sso_response()` matching the login page's logic.
Roughly 4 lines:

```python
provider = providers[0]

# If the lone provider is password-only, fall through to /login
# (the page renders the credential form). Don't auto-redirect to
# /auth/login?provider=... which would call start_login() and crash.
if getattr(provider, "supports_password", False):
    return None
```

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (commit `571092ee3`)
- Python 3.11.15
- Linux (Ubuntu)
- Tailscale 1.x

### Workaround (until upstream fix)

Apply the patch above manually to
`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py`. The
patch needs to be re-applied after every `hermes update` that touches
`dashboard_auth/`. A pre-built smoke test to detect regression:

```bash
curl -sSI http://<host>:<port>/ | head -3
# expect: HTTP/1.1 302 Found, Location: /login?next=%2F
# NOT /auth/login?provider=basic, NOT 500
```

### Why this matters

The dashboard is the GUI for managing config, API keys, MCP servers, and
the kanban board. The basic-auth path is the recommended setup for
single-operator Tailscale deployments (no OAuth client needed). A 500 on
the root path makes the dashboard unreachable without manual file edits
to switch off basic auth — which is itself not always possible if the
operator's only access is the dashboard.

items.title: [Bug]: GUI launch commands on Windows say exit_code: 0 but never actually open anything (Git Bash/MSYS rewriting /c before cmd.exe gets it)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

On Windows, commands that should launch detached GUI applications (for example `cmd /c start notepad`) report success inside Hermes (`exit_code: 0`) but the target application never actually opens.

After debugging this extensively, the issue appears to come from how Hermes wraps commands before execution.

Hermes executes commands through `bash -c`, and on Windows, MSYS/Git Bash automatically rewrites the `/c` argument before it reaches `cmd.exe`.

Because Hermes only checks the exit code of the wrapper process, the command is reported as successful even though the GUI process was never launched.

The main problem is silent false success reporting — Hermes says the application was launched even when nothing happened.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh install Hermes on Windows.
2. Confirm `hermes doctor` shows `terminal` available and no dependency warnings.
3. Run `hermes chat`.
4. Ask the agent:

```text id="a92v6r"
Open Notepad
```

5. Hermes executes:

```bash id="f20p8m"
cmd /c start notepad
```

6. Terminal tool returns:

```text id="w61c7n"
exit_code: 0
```

7. Hermes reports that Notepad was launched.
8. Check independently outside Hermes:

```bash id="k28r0u"
tasklist | findstr /I notepad
```

9. No `notepad.exe` process exists.

The same behavior can be reproduced directly without Hermes:

```bash id="3kg4zp"
bash -c "cmd /c start notepad"
tasklist | findstr /I notepad
```

No process gets created.

### Expected Behavior

When Hermes executes a command intended to launch a GUI application such as:

```bash id="6z8r1q"
cmd /c start notepad
```

the application should actually open.

If the process fails to launch, Hermes should detect that failure instead of reporting success based only on the wrapper process exit code.

---

### Actual Behavior

Hermes executes:

```bash id="n45s9t"
cmd /c start notepad
```

The terminal tool returns:

```text id="d73u0w"
exit_code: 0
```

Hermes reports the application launched successfully.

However, the application never opens.

Manual verification:

```bash id="e11m2y"
tasklist | findstr /I notepad
```

returns nothing.

So the command silently fails while Hermes reports success.

---

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/su2x2
agent.log    https://paste.rs/HXw2N
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/42X4e
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 build 10.0.26200.8737

### Python Version

3.12.10

### Hermes Version

v0.17.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`tools/environments/base.py` wraps commands using:

```bash id="x81l5f"
bash -c "<command>"
```

MSYS-based Bash (both system Git Bash and bundled MinGit Bash) automatically rewrites POSIX-looking arguments.

When Hermes runs:

```bash id="t64j3n"
cmd /c start notepad
```

the `/c` argument is treated like a Unix-style path and rewritten before `cmd.exe` receives it.

As a result:

* `cmd.exe` never receives a valid `/c` flag
* `start notepad` never executes correctly
* the GUI process is never spawned
* Bash exits normally
* Hermes sees only `exit_code: 0` from the Bash wrapper and reports success

Minimal reproduction outside Hermes:

Fails:

```bash id="u92k1d"
bash -c "cmd /c start notepad"
```

Works:

```bash id="j08n4p"
bash -c "cmd //c start notepad"
```

Works:

```bash id="r65c2z"
bash -c "powershell -Command \"Start-Process notepad\""
```

Works:

```bash id="m18f0v"
bash -c "export MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='/c'; cmd /c start notepad"
```

This confirms the issue comes from MSYS argument rewriting before `cmd.exe` processes the command.

---

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Possible fixes:

**1. Rewrite `/c` to `//c` on Windows before passing commands through Bash**

```bash id="h77n3k"
cmd /c ...
```

becomes:

```bash id="z33p9s"
cmd //c ...
```

---

**2. Set `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` before spawning Bash**

Exclude `/c` from automatic MSYS argument conversion.

---

**3. Route GUI launches through PowerShell instead**

Instead of:

```bash id="l49q8a"
cmd /c start notepad
```

use:

```bash id="o21r7f"
powershell -Command "Start-Process notepad"
```

---

**4. Do not assume `exit_code: 0` means the GUI process launched successfully**

Hermes currently checks only the wrapper process exit code.

There should be some verification step to confirm the detached process was actually created.

## Summary

When switching models via `/model` from Telegram (gateway), the handler persists `model.base_url` in `config.yaml`. For `anthropic_messages` models (e.g. `minimax-m3` on opencode-go) the URL is stored **without `/v1`** (correct for that mode — the Anthropic SDK appends `/v1/messages`). When the user then switches to a `chat_completions` model (e.g. `glm-5.2`), the stale URL wins the config override and every non-MiniMax model returns **HTTP 404**.

## Reproduction

**Config:**
```yaml
model:
  default: minimax-m3
  provider: opencode-go
```

**Steps:**
1. From Telegram, send `/model minimax-m3` → works (anthropic_messages)
2. From Telegram, send `/model glm-5.2` → 404
3. Check `~/.hermes/config.yaml` → `model.base_url` is now `https://opencode.ai/zen/go` (without `/v1`)

**Log:**
```
OpenAI client created ... provider=opencode-go base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go model=glm-5.2
Streaming failed: <!DOCTYPE html>... <title>Not Found | opencode</title>...
API call failed (attempt 1/3): HTTP 404 — Not Found | opencode
```

**Expected:** `base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` (with `/v1`), HTTP 200

**Workaround:** Delete `model.base_url` from `config.yaml` and restart gateway.

## Root cause

`gateway/slash_commands.py:1356-1357` persists `result.base_url` on every `/model` switch:
```python
if result.base_url:
    _persist_model_cfg["base_url"] = result.base_url
```

For `anthropic_messages` models, `result.base_url` is the URL **without `/v1`** (stripped by `_resolve_runtime_from_pool_entry`). On the next switch to a `chat_completions` model, `_resolve_runtime_from_pool_entry` reads that stale URL from config and uses it unconditionally:

```python
# hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:391-394
if configured_provider == provider and pool_url_is_default:
    cfg_base_url = str(model_cfg.get("base_url") or "").strip().rstrip("/")
    if cfg_base_url:
        base_url = cfg_base_url   # ← stale URL without /v1 wins
```

The `pool_url_is_default` guard only checks the **pool's** URL matches the `inference_base_url`, not the **config's** URL.

## Affected models

All 19 non-MiniMax models on opencode-go: `glm-5.2`, `glm-5.1`, `glm-5`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-k2.5`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.5-plus`, `mimo-v2-pro`, `mimo-v2-omni`, `mimo-v2.5-pro`, `mimo-v2.5`, `hy3-preview`.

Only reproducible via Telegram/gateway `/model`. CLI `hermes chat -m <model>` works because it does not persist `model.base_url`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.17.0, commit `caf4dcc7a`
- Provider: opencode-go
- Platform: Telegram gateway
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS

## Proposed fix

PR #56157 — scope the config override to opencode-zen/opencode-go: only honour `model.base_url` when it matches the provider's current `inference_base_url`. Otherwise keep the pool default (with `/v1`).

## Related

- #16878 — same bug family (api_mode derivation on /model switch)
- #15319 — same root cause in delegate_tool.py
- #53251 — complementary fix for runtime_override staleness

### Bug Description

## Summary

While configuring Hermes to use the OpenAI Codex App Server runtime, I found confusing behavior around the runtime configuration.

Initially I configured:

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-5.5
  provider: openai-codex
  base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
  api_mode: codex_app_server
```

Hermes continued using the `codex_responses` transport and every request timed out after 90 seconds.

After investigating the source code, I discovered references to `model.openai_runtime`.

Changing the configuration to:

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-5.5
  provider: openai-codex
  base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
  openai_runtime: codex_app_server
```

immediately solved the problem.

I'm not sure whether this is expected behavior or a documentation issue, but it was extremely difficult to discover because the configuration key is not obvious.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with:

```yaml
model:
  default: gpt-5.5
  provider: openai-codex
  base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex
  api_mode: codex_app_server
```

2. Run:

```bash
hermes -z "Respond only Ok"
```

3. Wait about 90 seconds.

4. Hermes times out with:

```
Non-streaming API call timed out after 90s...
```

### Expected Behavior

If `api_mode: codex_app_server` is not intended to enable the Codex App Server runtime, the documentation should clearly state that `openai_runtime` must be used instead.

If it is intended to work, then Hermes should switch to the Codex App Server runtime automatically.

### Actual Behavior

Hermes continued using the `codex_responses` transport and every request timed out after approximately 90 seconds.

Changing the configuration to:

```yaml
model:
  openai_runtime: codex_app_server
```

immediately resolved the problem without any other changes.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report: https://paste.rs/uZ6r3
agent.log: https://paste.rs/Tp8D6
gateway.log: https://paste.rs/HmGRL
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

3.12.3

### Hermes Version

0.17.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
The same ChatGPT Business account works correctly with the official Codex CLI (v0.142.5) using GPT-5.5.

The issue was only reproducible when Hermes was configured with `api_mode: codex_app_server`.

Switching to `openai_runtime: codex_app_server` resolved the issue immediately.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

While investigating I found references to:

- `_maybe_apply_codex_app_server_runtime()`
- `model.openai_runtime == "codex_app_server"`

This suggests that runtime selection is controlled by `openai_runtime`, not `api_mode`.

Because of that, users may reasonably configure `api_mode` expecting the runtime to change, while Hermes continues using the `codex_responses` transport.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Either:

- document that the Codex App Server runtime is enabled through `model.openai_runtime`, or

- accept `api_mode: codex_app_server` as an alias, or

- emit a warning when `api_mode: codex_app_server` is configured but ignored.

## Feature Description

Add native Windows system notification (toast notification) support to the Hermes GUI/TUI when the gateway receives an incoming message from a connected messaging platform (Telegram, Discord, etc.).

## Motivation

When using Hermes with the Telegram gateway, the Hermes process runs in the background. Currently, the only notification mechanism is:

- **Terminal bell** (`bell_on_complete`) — just a sound, no visual indicator, easily missed
- **Telegram Desktop notifications** — works but requires a separate app running

For users who primarily interact through the Hermes GUI/TUI, there is **no visual cue** on the Windows taskbar or notification center that a new message has arrived and is being processed. The user has to manually switch to the Hermes window to check.

## Proposed Solution

Add a new config option (e.g. `display.desktop_notifications: true`) that, when enabled, triggers a **Windows toast notification** when:

1. The gateway receives a new inbound message from any platform
2. The agent finishes processing and sends a response back

Implementation options:
- **Python**: Use `win10toast`, `winotify`, or `plyer` library to send native Windows toast notifications
- **PowerShell fallback**: Call `[Windows.UI.Notifications.ToastNotificationManager]` via subprocess

```yaml
display:
  desktop_notifications: true  # Windows toast on new messages
```

## Use Case

1. User runs `hermes gateway run` (or installs as Windows login item)
2. Hermes GUI is minimized to taskbar
3. Someone sends a message to the Telegram bot
4. **A Windows toast notification pops up** showing the sender and message preview
5. User clicks the notification to switch to the Hermes window

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes: latest (GUI desktop app)

## Alternatives Considered

- Relying on Telegram Desktop notifications — requires running a separate app
- Terminal bell only — no visual indicator, easy to miss
- Taskbar flash — less informative than toast notifications

items.body:
## Description

After upgrading to latest `main`, the Web UI TUI console continuously logs:

```
error: unknown method: pet.cells
```

## Root Cause

The TUI frontend (`ui-tui/src/app/usePet.ts`) polls `pet.cells` RPC every few seconds via `setInterval`. The gateway backend (`tui_gateway/server.py`) has no `@method("pet.cells")` handler registered — it's an unimplemented feature.

The frontend does `catch {}` on the RPC failure (line 246: `// cosmetic — ignore RPC failures`) but the error still surfaces to the console/browser because it's thrown during the `rpc()` call before the catch.

## Impact

- Error floods the TUI console every ~3 seconds
- Confuses users into thinking the upgrade failed
- The pixel-pet animation feature is only half-implemented

## Suggested Fix

Either:

1. **Add the missing RPC handler** (backend side)
2. **Gate the frontend feature behind a feature flag** until the backend is ready — currently the polling starts unconditionally regardless of whether the backend supports it

## Workaround

Users can hot-patch `tui_gateway/server.py` with a stub:

```python
@method("pet.cells")
def _(rid, params: dict) -> dict:
    return _ok(rid, {"enabled": False, "slug": "", "frames": [], "scale": 0})
```

## Environment

- Hermes v0.17.0 (main @ f2a528fb5)
- Server: Alibaba Cloud Linux 3

items.body:
## Feature request

Hermes' Slack adapter should support Slack's richer Block Kit rendering path for assistant replies, not only plain `chat_postMessage(text=..., mrkdwn=True)`.

Today the Slack adapter converts standard Markdown to Slack `mrkdwn` and posts it as plain text. That works for basic emphasis, links, blockquotes, and code blocks, but it does not fully match what Slack can now render via Block Kit `markdown` blocks or `rich_text` blocks.

## User-visible problem

When using Hermes from Slack, responses containing common Markdown structures do not render as well as other Slack bots that use richer Slack message payloads:

```md
**Bold heading**

- first bullet
- second bullet

1. first ordered item
2. second ordered item

> quoted note

[Slack docs](https://docs.slack.dev/)

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Activation | 42% |
```

Expected behavior in Slack:
- `**bold**` renders as bold
- unordered and ordered lists render as native lists
- block quotes render as quotes
- Markdown links render as links
- Markdown tables render as formatted tables when Slack supports them
- code blocks and inline code continue to work

Actual behavior today:
- Hermes mostly relies on `mrkdwn=True` text payloads
- some Markdown has to be translated to Slack-specific syntax
- native lists/tables are not consistently rendered as native Slack rich text
- long analytical Slack replies are harder to read than equivalent output from bots using Block Kit `markdown` or `rich_text` blocks

## Current implementation

The current Slack send path is in `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`:

```py
formatted = self.format_message(content)
chunks = self.truncate_message(formatted, self.MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH)
...
kwargs = {
    "channel": chat_id,
    "text": chunk,
    "mrkdwn": True,
}
await self._get_client(chat_id).chat_postMessage(**kwargs)
```

`SlackAdapter.format_message()` protects code regions and converts selected Markdown constructs to Slack `mrkdwn`, but the final payload is still plain `text`.

Related prior issue:
- #18918 focused specifically on rendering Markdown pipe tables as Slack Block Kit tables.
- This request is broader: use Slack's richer Markdown/rich-text rendering mode for the whole assistant response where possible, including lists, tables, quotes, links, code, and fallback behavior.

## Proposed solution

Add a Slack rendering layer that chooses the best supported payload shape:

1. Prefer Block Kit `markdown` blocks for eligible assistant replies.
   - Use `blocks: [{"type": "markdown", "text": content}]` where supported.
   - Preserve `text` as notification/fallback text.
   - This should allow Slack-native rendering for Markdown lists, tables, links, quotes, code blocks, etc.

2. Fall back to `rich_text` blocks when more control is needed.
   - Useful if `markdown` blocks have workspace/client/API limitations.
   - Could map assistant output into `rich_text_section`, `rich_text_list`, `rich_text_quote`, and `rich_text_preformatted` elements.

3. Fall back to today's `text + mrkdwn=True` path when block rendering is unavailable or content exceeds Slack limits.
   - This preserves compatibility with existing Slack behavior.
   - Keep current chunking and code-block preservation semantics.

4. Support slash-command ephemeral replies and message edits consistently.
   - `chat_postEphemeral` and response_url replies may need compatible `blocks` support.
   - `chat_update` should preserve the same rendering strategy when editing streamed/final messages.

## Implementation notes / constraints

- Respect Slack block count and text length limits.
- Preserve `reply_broadcast`, `thread_ts`, assistant status clearing, and bot-message timestamp tracking.
- Avoid regressing code blocks, inline code, Slack mentions/entities, and existing Slack links.
- Keep a safe fallback for notifications and clients that do not render the new blocks.
- Consider a config gate if maintainers want a gradual rollout, e.g. `gateway.slack.rich_markdown_blocks: true`.

## Suggested tests

- Unit tests for choosing `markdown` block vs fallback text path.
- Payload tests for bold, unordered lists, ordered lists, quote, Markdown links, inline code, code block, and Markdown table.
- Fallback tests for oversized content, unsupported/malformed content, and multiple chunks.
- Coverage for `send`, `send_private_notice`, and `edit_message` if all can emit rich Slack payloads.
- Regression tests to ensure existing `format_message()` behavior still works in fallback mode.

## References

- Slack formatting docs: https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/formatting-message-text/
- Slack Markdown block: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/markdown-block/
- Slack rich text block: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/rich-text-block/

### Problem or Use Case

Using Hermes with the Vertex AI OpenAI-compatible endpoint is harder than it needs to be.

The main issue is that this endpoint does not behave like a typical static API-key provider. It requires short-lived OAuth access tokens, so users need some way to refresh credentials automatically.

Right now, that creates a confusing setup experience:
- it looks like `base_url + api_key` should be enough
- users may assume they can paste a temporary token into `api_key`
- users may assume a regular Google API key will work
- in practice, users end up needing a custom token provider, custom runtime wiring, or a local proxy

This makes Vertex feel much less straightforward than other OpenAI-compatible providers, even when the endpoint itself is supported.

### Proposed Solution

Hermes should provide a first-class way to use Vertex OpenAI-compatible endpoints with automatically refreshed OAuth credentials.

Any of the following would solve the problem:

1. Add a dedicated Vertex provider mode
   - accept ADC / service account credentials
   - refresh OAuth access tokens automatically before requests
   - expose a clear config example

2. Officially support dynamic token providers in provider config
   - allow `api_key` (or equivalent auth field) to be a callable / token resolver
   - document this explicitly for Vertex
   - provide a minimal working example using `google-auth`

3. Document an official proxy pattern
   - if the recommended approach is to run a local proxy that injects refreshed bearer tokens, provide a small reference implementation

At minimum, the docs should clearly explain that Vertex OpenAI-compatible auth is not the same as a normal long-lived API key flow.

None

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram compact /reasoning level commands are rejected in groups
items.body:
## Summary

Telegram can emit `/reasoning` level selections as a compact slash command such as `/reasoningmedium` instead of `/reasoning medium` in group chats. The gateway currently treats that as an unknown command.

## Reproduction

On current `upstream/main`:

```python
from gateway.platforms.base import MessageEvent

e = MessageEvent(text="/reasoningmedium")
print(e.get_command(), repr(e.get_command_args()))
```

Actual:

```text
reasoningmedium ''
```

Expected:

```text
reasoning 'medium'
```

The same issue applies to group bot mentions, e.g. `/reasoningxhigh@BotName --global` should dispatch to `/reasoning` with args `xhigh --global`.

## Impact

Users selecting/typing compact Telegram commands in groups get:

```text
Unknown command /reasoningmedium. Type /commands to see what's available...
```

instead of changing the reasoning effort.

items.title: feat(skill): add repo-sdd-forge for repository-specific SDD and Ouroboros harness
items.body:
## Summary

Add a new Hermes skill, tentatively named `repo-sdd-forge`, that bootstraps and maintains **repository-specific SDD**.

This should not be a generic “write a spec/tasks document” skill. It should first inspect the target repository deeply, extract the repo's product/domain/architecture kernel, then create an AI-readable SDD operating manual and propose a lightweight loop harness.

The intended output is a repo-local AI operating manual, for example:

```text
.hermes/sdd/
  README.md
  repo-map.md
  domain-kernel.md
  context.md
  architecture.md
  risk-map.md
  verification.md
  adr/
  specs/
  tasks/
  reviews/
  harness/
```

Future agents should be able to read this before large work, avoid contradicting prior decisions, create specs/tasks consistently, and reconcile docs after implementation.

---

## Motivation

Long AI-assisted development drifts when the agent relies on transient chat context, partial memory, or shallow code search.

Existing skills cover pieces of the flow:

| Existing skill | Covers |
|---|---|
| `writing-plans` | implementation planning |
| `plan` | saving actionable plans |
| `subagent-driven-development` | task execution via subagents |
| `test-driven-development` | RED/GREEN/REFACTOR discipline |
| `codebase-inspection` | repo review and engineering assessment |
| `requesting-code-review` | quality review |

Missing layer:

1. study a repository as a product/system,
2. extract durable domain and architecture knowledge,
3. create repo-local SDD docs,
4. propose a loop harness,
5. reconcile docs after implementation.

Failure modes this should reduce:

- AI implements plausible features that violate product identity.
- Subagents drift because they share no repo-specific operating manual.
- Architecture decisions are rediscovered or contradicted.
- Specs/tasks are written without understanding repo history.
- Docs rot because implementation is not reconciled back into them.
- Future sessions require expensive re-discovery.

---

## Core concept

The skill should implement an **Ouroboros loop**:

```text
Observe repo
→ Model repo
→ Specify work
→ Execute tasks
→ Verify
→ Reconcile docs
→ Improve harness
→ repeat
```

The skill's main job is to create and maintain the repo model and the reconciliation loop.

---

## Goals

### 1. Deeply inspect the target repository before writing docs

Before writing any SDD docs, inspect:

- repo path
- branch
- dirty state
- README
- docs
- package manifests
- framework/tooling config
- app entrypoints
- routes/pages/API endpoints
- domain models
- services
- tests
- CI config
- recent git history
- hotspots / large files
- verification commands

The skill must not write SDD from user intent alone.

### 2. Extract repo-specific kernels

The skill should produce structured understanding of the repo:

| Kernel | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Product thesis | What this repo is building, and what it is not |
| Core user loop | The repeated user/system workflow the repo serves |
| Domain language | Terms the repo uses, including user-facing Korean terms where relevant |
| Architecture boundaries | Which layer owns what |
| Decision history | Existing or inferred ADR-level choices |
| Verification map | What commands prove the repo still works |
| Risk map | Files/areas likely to break or drift |

### 3. Create repo-local SDD scaffold

Default output path:

```text
.hermes/sdd/
```

Proposed structure:

```text
.hermes/sdd/
  README.md
  repo-map.md
  domain-kernel.md
  context.md
  architecture.md
  risk-map.md
  verification.md
  adr/
    _template.md
  specs/
    _template.md
  tasks/
    _template.md
  reviews/
    _template.md
  harness/
    loop.md
    gates.md
    check.py
```

The structure should be AI-first but still human-readable.

### 4. Evidence-tag important claims

Avoid hallucinating repo facts. Every important repo claim should be tagged as one of:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Evidence-backed` | confirmed from code/docs/git/user-provided repo facts |
| `Inferred` | likely based on multiple clues, but not directly stated |
| `Proposed` | recommended by the agent, not yet accepted |
| `Needs decision` | requires user/product owner confirmation |

Example:

```markdown
| Claim | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop should be operation-room first | Evidence-backed | user profile, existing product memory, route naming |
| Offline-first is a desired future direction | Proposed | no direct repo evidence |
| Firebase owns durable app state | Evidence-backed | `lib/firebase/*`, config files |
```

### 5. Propose loop harness, not just docs

Generate a lightweight harness proposal under:

```text
.hermes/sdd/harness/
```

Minimum docs:

```text
harness/loop.md
harness/gates.md
```

Optional advisory script:

```text
harness/check.py
```

The harness should define when SDD is required and when it can be skipped.

---

## Non-goals

This issue should **not** implement:

- full CI-enforced SDD from day one
- heavyweight enterprise documentation framework
- automatic code implementation
- automatic PR creation
- automatic architecture decisions without evidence
- replacement for `writing-plans`, `subagent-driven-development`, or `test-driven-development`
- full static analysis of every file in large repos
- mandatory SDD for trivial one-line changes

The goal is a practical repo-specific AI operating manual, not documentation bureaucracy.

---

## Skill modes

### Mode A: Bootstrap

Triggered by prompts such as:

```text
이 repo SDD 부트스트랩해
이 리포지토리 뼛속깊이 읽고 SDD 만들어
repo-sdd-forge bootstrap
```

Expected behavior:

1. Inspect repo state.
2. Read key docs/config/source/test files.
3. Optionally dispatch read-only subagents for separate lanes.
4. Extract product/domain/architecture kernels.
5. Generate `.hermes/sdd/` scaffold.
6. Mark uncertain claims as `Inferred`, `Proposed`, or `Needs decision`.
7. Propose loop harness.
8. Report created files and open questions.

### Mode B: Feature Spec

Triggered by prompts such as:

```text
이 기능 SDD로 잡고 가자
이 기능 spec/tasks 만들어
repo-sdd-forge feature <feature>
```

Expected behavior:

1. Read `.hermes/sdd/README.md`.
2. Read relevant `domain-kernel.md`, `architecture.md`, `context.md`, and ADRs.
3. Search for related existing specs/tasks.
4. Create or update a feature spec.
5. Derive tasks from the spec.
6. Include acceptance criteria and verification commands.
7. Identify ADR conflicts or missing decisions.

### Mode C: Reconcile

Triggered by prompts such as:

```text
이번 변경 SDD reconcile 해
구현된 거 문서랑 맞춰
repo-sdd-forge reconcile
```

Expected behavior:

1. Inspect git diff and changed files.
2. Compare implementation against relevant specs/tasks.
3. Update task statuses.
4. Record actual verification results.
5. Update specs if implementation intentionally diverged.
6. Draft ADR if a meaningful decision was made.
7. Update risk map / architecture notes if repo understanding changed.

### Mode D: Harness Review

Triggered by prompts such as:

```text
이 repo SDD 하네스 리뷰해
루프 하네스 너무 무거운지 봐
repo-sdd-forge harness-review
```

Expected behavior:

1. Review existing `.hermes/sdd/harness/*`.
2. Identify missing gates.
3. Identify overly heavy gates.
4. Recommend which checks should remain soft, script-based, or CI-enforced.
5. Suggest improvements to `check.py` if present.

---

## Deep repo inspection strategy

Prefer read-only investigation before writing.

Required checks:

```bash
git status --short
git branch --show-current
git log --oneline -10
```

Inspect likely files when present:

```text
README.md
AGENTS.md
HERMES.md
CLAUDE.md
package.json
pnpm-lock.yaml
pyproject.toml
requirements.txt
docker-compose*.yml
.github/workflows/*
docs/**
src/**
app/**
pages/**
lib/**
backend/**
frontend/**
tests/**
```

Use Hermes file tools (`search_files`, `read_file`) rather than raw `cat` / `grep` where possible.

---

## Optional subagent lanes

For larger repositories, the skill may dispatch read-only subagents:

| Lane | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Product/Domain lane | Extract product thesis, user loop, copy/tone, user-facing concepts |
| Architecture lane | Identify entrypoints, data flow, boundaries, dependencies |
| Verification lane | Identify tests, build commands, smoke checks, CI |
| History lane | Inspect git/docs for prior decisions and drift |

Constraint:

> Subagents should report findings only. The controller session writes final SDD docs to keep structure and evidence tags consistent.

---

## Document requirements

### `.hermes/sdd/README.md`

Purpose: entrypoint for future AI agents.

Should include:

```markdown
# SDD Operating Manual

## Read Order for AI Agents

1. `domain-kernel.md`
2. `architecture.md`
3. `context.md`
4. relevant `adr/*`
5. relevant `specs/*`
6. relevant `tasks/*`

## When SDD Is Required

Use SDD for:
- multi-file features
- product/domain changes
- architecture changes
- database/schema changes
- subagent-driven implementation
- changes touching known risk areas

SDD may be skipped for:
- typos
- one-line fixes
- mechanical formatting
- throwaway experiments that will not be merged
```

### `repo-map.md`

Purpose: practical codebase map.

Include:

- repo identity
- stack
- main directories
- entrypoints
- data stores
- API surfaces
- tests
- deployment/runtime notes
- hotspots

### `domain-kernel.md`

Purpose: product essence.

Include:

- product thesis
- what this repo is not
- core user loop
- user-facing terms
- tone/product constraints
- non-negotiables
- known product risks

### `context.md`

Purpose: AI-readable glossary and ubiquitous language.

Include:

- repo-specific terms
- abbreviations
- Korean/English naming mapping where relevant
- terms to avoid
- ambiguous terms needing clarification

### `architecture.md`

Purpose: architecture boundaries.

Include:

- layer responsibilities
- data ownership
- external services
- integration points
- state flow
- known architectural hazards
- extension points
- anti-patterns

### `risk-map.md`

Purpose: prevent blind changes.

Include:

- fragile files
- oversized files
- frequently changed areas
- security-sensitive areas
- stateful logic
- migration-sensitive areas
- test gaps

### `verification.md`

Purpose: know how to prove changes.

Include:

- install/setup commands
- test commands
- lint commands
- build commands
- smoke checks
- route checks
- deploy checks if applicable
- known flaky/slow tests

### `adr/_template.md`

```markdown
# ADR-NNNN: <decision>

## Status
Proposed | Accepted | Deprecated | Superseded | Inferred | Needs decision

## Context

## Decision

## Evidence

## Consequences

## Alternatives Considered

## Follow-ups
```

### `specs/_template.md`

```markdown
# Spec: <feature>

## Status
Draft | Accepted | Implementing | Implemented | Deprecated

## Problem

## Goals

## Non-goals

## User / Operator Flow

## Requirements

## Acceptance Criteria

## Architecture Notes

## ADR / Context Links

## Verification Plan

## Open Questions
```

### `tasks/_template.md`

```markdown
# Tasks: <feature>

Spec: `../specs/<feature>.md`
Status: pending | in-progress | complete

## Task 1: <name>

- Depends on:
- Files:
- Steps:
- Acceptance:
- Verification:
- Status:
- Notes:
```

---

## Harness design

### Soft harness

Generate advisory instructions:

```markdown
For any multi-file feature:
1. Read `.hermes/sdd/README.md`.
2. Find or create a spec.
3. Derive tasks.
4. Verify each task.
5. Reconcile docs after implementation.
```

### Check harness

Optional advisory script:

```text
.hermes/sdd/harness/check.py
```

Suggested checks:

- feature spec exists
- tasks file links to spec
- acceptance criteria exist
- verification command exists
- completed task includes verification result
- architecture-sensitive change has ADR or explicit note
- `Needs decision` items are not silently treated as accepted

Example CLI:

```bash
python .hermes/sdd/harness/check.py --feature desktop-operation-room
python .hermes/sdd/harness/check.py --changed
```

### CI harness

Out of scope for MVP, but docs may mention future CI integration.

Potential future check:

```bash
python .hermes/sdd/harness/check.py --changed --ci
```

CI should only be introduced after the repo-specific harness proves useful.

---

## Implementation plan

### Phase 1: Create the Hermes skill

Add a user-local skill first:

```text
~/.hermes/skills/software-development/repo-sdd-forge/SKILL.md
```

If dogfood succeeds, promote to in-repo skill later:

```text
skills/software-development/repo-sdd-forge/SKILL.md
```

Initial `SKILL.md` should include:

- overview
- when to use
- when not to use
- modes
- bootstrap workflow
- evidence tagging rules
- document structure
- harness levels
- subagent lane guidance
- pitfalls
- verification checklist

### Phase 2: Add templates

Add template files:

```text
templates/README.md
templates/repo-map.md
templates/domain-kernel.md
templates/context.md
templates/architecture.md
templates/risk-map.md
templates/verification.md
templates/adr.md
templates/spec.md
templates/tasks.md
templates/harness-loop.md
templates/harness-gates.md
```

Templates should be short and structured. Avoid huge boilerplate that makes every repo look the same.

### Phase 3: Add optional check script

Add:

```text
scripts/sdd_check.py
```

MVP checks:

- `.hermes/sdd/README.md` exists
- required core docs exist
- every spec has `Goals`, `Non-goals`, `Acceptance Criteria`, `Verification Plan`
- every task file references a spec
- completed tasks include verification notes
- ADR statuses are valid

The script should be advisory at first, not CI-blocking.

### Phase 4: Trial on one real repo

Candidate repos:

| Repo | Why |
|---|---|
| Dark Motivation | strong product identity, high risk of generic AI drift |
| TrendRank | product strategy + content/data workflows need clear decision boundaries |
| Quant-X | complex architecture, gates, risk model, multiple pipelines |
| Desk | cross-repo boundary with Quant-X, context/collector concerns |

Recommendation: dogfood on **Dark Motivation** first because product identity drift is the most obvious failure mode.

### Phase 5: Reconcile after first real use

After one real implementation cycle:

1. Run bootstrap.
2. Use generated SDD for a feature.
3. Implement feature with normal Hermes workflow.
4. Run reconcile.
5. Patch the skill based on what was too vague/heavy/missing.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `repo-sdd-forge` skill exists and can be loaded.
- [ ] Skill clearly distinguishes generic SDD from repo-specific SDD.
- [ ] Skill requires repo inspection before writing SDD.
- [ ] Skill defines four modes: Bootstrap, Feature Spec, Reconcile, Harness Review.
- [ ] Skill requires evidence tagging for important claims.
- [ ] Skill defines the default `.hermes/sdd/` structure.
- [ ] Skill includes templates for core docs.
- [ ] Skill proposes the Ouroboros loop.
- [ ] Skill includes soft/check/CI harness levels.
- [ ] Skill documents when SDD can be skipped.
- [ ] Skill includes subagent read-only lane guidance.
- [ ] Optional `sdd_check.py` exists or is explicitly deferred.
- [ ] Skill has a verification checklist.
- [ ] First dogfood repo is selected.

---

## Open questions

1. Should the default output path be `.hermes/sdd/` or `docs/sdd/`?
   - Proposal: `.hermes/sdd/` by default, because this is primarily AI operating context.

2. Should generated SDD docs be committed to the repo?
   - Proposal: yes for long-lived product repos, no for throwaway/spike repos.

3. Should the skill create docs immediately, or first present a proposed scaffold?
   - Proposal: bootstrap mode may write docs if explicitly requested. Otherwise present scaffold first.

4. Should `sdd_check.py` be included in MVP?
   - Proposal: include a minimal advisory checker, but do not wire to CI.

5. Should ADRs be generated automatically?
   - Proposal: only as `Inferred` or `Proposed` unless directly evidence-backed.

6. Should this eventually integrate with `subagent-driven-development`?
   - Proposal: yes, but not by replacing it. `repo-sdd-forge` prepares context/spec/tasks; `subagent-driven-development` executes.

7. Should this be user-local first or promoted into Hermes core skills?
   - Proposal: user-local first. Promote after dogfood.

---

## Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Skill writes confident but false repo claims | Require evidence tags |
| Too many docs become unreadable | Keep README read order and concise core docs |
| SDD becomes bureaucracy | Allow skip for trivial changes |
| Docs rot after implementation | Reconcile mode |
| Subagents produce inconsistent docs | Subagents investigate only; controller writes final docs |
| Harness blocks useful work | Start with soft/check harness only; defer CI |

---

## Suggested MVP scope

MVP should include:

1. `SKILL.md`
2. document structure definition
3. evidence tagging
4. bootstrap mode
5. feature spec mode
6. reconcile mode
7. templates
8. no CI
9. optional lightweight `sdd_check.py`

Defer:

- CI enforcement
- GitHub issue/PR automation
- automatic task execution
- deep metrics dashboards
- complex doc rendering

---

## Short version

Build `repo-sdd-forge`: a Hermes skill that deeply inspects a repository, extracts its product/domain/architecture kernel, creates `.hermes/sdd/` docs, and proposes an Ouroboros loop harness so future AI development remains aligned with repo reality instead of drifting.

items.title: restore_primary_runtime() swaps in a cross-provider credential, sending the wrong model name to the wrong endpoint

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

`restore_primary_runtime()` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1174-1201`) re-selects a credential from `agent._credential_pool` when resuming the primary provider after a fallback, and calls `agent._swap_credential(entry)` with no check that the entry's provider matches the runtime being restored:

```python
pool = getattr(agent, "_credential_pool", None)
if pool is not None and pool.has_available():
    entry = pool.select()
    if entry is not None and entry_key:
        agent._swap_credential(entry)   # no provider check
```

If the pool holds a leftover credential from a previously-activated fallback, this overwrites `base_url`/`api_key` with the *fallback's* provider while `agent.model` stays set to the primary's model. The request goes out with the wrong model name at the wrong endpoint, which that provider correctly rejects.

Same root cause as #52777 (checkout-side pool is provider-blind). **PR #52799** (open) fixes this pattern in `switch_model()`, but its diff never touches `restore_primary_runtime()` — this call site is still unguarded.

## Reproduction

Config: `model.provider: custom` (local OpenAI-compatible endpoint), `model: ornith-35b`, single `fallback_providers` entry for `deepseek`.

```
INFO  client created (restore_primary) provider=custom base_url=https://<primary-host>/v1 model=ornith-35b
INFO  client created (credential_rotation) provider=custom base_url=https://api.deepseek.com/v1 model=ornith-35b
INFO  Restore re-selected pool entry 6bcafe (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
INFO  Primary runtime restored for new turn: ornith-35b (custom)
...
INFO  Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message':
      'The supported API model names are deepseek-v4-pro or deepseek-v4-flash,
      but you passed ornith-35b.', ...}}
WARNING  Credential pool provider mismatch: pool=deepseek, agent=custom — skipping
         pool mutation to avoid cross-provider contamination
INFO  Fallback activated: ornith-35b → deepseek-v4-pro (deepseek)
```

The existing mismatch guard *does* fire — but only after the bad request already went out and failed, same pattern #52777 describes. Reproduced twice in one session (once after a transient 502 fallback, once after a compression-triggered turn rollover); identical sequence both times.

## Impact

Every turn that resumes a custom/local-endpoint primary after any fallback activation gets silently re-routed to the fallback with a broken request. The primary appears to "try and immediately fail" on every subsequent turn — but the request never actually reaches the primary provider at all.

## Suggested fix

Apply the same provider-match helper #52799 introduces (`credential_pool_matches_provider()`) at `agent_runtime_helpers.py:1183`, guarding `agent._swap_credential(entry)` the same way `switch_model()` is being guarded. On mismatch, keep the snapshot's own `rt["api_key"]`/`client_kwargs` (already restored correctly a few lines earlier) instead of skipping recovery outright.

## Environment
- hermes-agent @ `43edbae6` (2026-07-01)
- Custom provider (local OpenAI-compatible endpoint) as primary, `deepseek` as sole `fallback_providers` entry

### Bug Description

When working with multiple chat sessions at the same time in the Hermes Desktop app, a queued message intended for one session can be delivered into a different session.

Concretely: I queue one or more messages in Session A while the agent is still busy/streaming. Before that queue drains, I switch the active view to another session (Session B). When Session A's queue flushes, the queued message(s) are fired into the currently-focused session (Session B) instead of Session A, where they were composed and queued.

In other words, the pending message queue appears to be routed to "the currently active/foreground session" at flush time rather than to the session the message was originally enqueued for. This misroutes user input across sessions — a queued prompt can be sent to the wrong agent/conversation.

Note: this is Desktop-only. The terminal / TUI does not exhibit this — it only happens in the Hermes Desktop app where multiple sessions can be switched between in the UI.

1. Open the Hermes Desktop app and start 3 chat sessions.

3. Before Session A's queue has drained, switch the active/foreground view to a different session (Session B).
4. Wait for Session A's queue to flush.

Each queued message must be delivered to the exact session it was composed and enqueued in. Switching the foreground/active session must not change the destination of already-queued messages. The queued message is occasionally fired into whatever session is currently active/focused at flush time, not the session it was queued in. items.title: Interrupt-protected compression + default busy_input_mode=interrupt can fork multiple orphaned compression siblings from one stale parent during a message burst

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

With the default `busy_input_mode: interrupt`, a burst of rapid gateway messages arriving while context compression is in flight can trigger **multiple independent compression events on the same (stale) parent session**, producing several orphaned one-shot sibling continuations instead of a single clean parent → child chain. Only the last sibling ends up being the "real" live continuation; the earlier siblings are dead-end forks that hold a couple of turns each and are otherwise invisible/wasted.

This looks like an unintended interaction between the fix for #23975 (compression made interrupt-immune via `aux_interrupt_protection` / `agent/auxiliary_client.py`) and the gateway's default `interrupt` busy-input mode, which does **not** wait for an in-flight (now uninterruptible) compression to finish and its session-id rotation to propagate before starting the next turn.

## Observed Logs (sanitized session ids)

```text
15:14:18 [S0] agent.conversation_compression: context compression started: session=S0 messages=1613 tokens=~501,789
15:14:18 [S0] agent.auxiliary_client: Auxiliary compression: using auto ...
15:16:03 [S1] agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=S1 messages=1613->1161
15:16:14 [S1] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=interrupted_during_api_call ... session=S1
15:16:14 [S1] gateway.run: Session split detected: S0 → S1 (compression)
15:16:14 [S0] gateway.run: Agent cache invalidated for session <key>: message_count changed (1614 -> 1617), possible cross-process write
15:16:19 [S0] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=S0 ...            # <-- new turn still bound to S0, not S1
...
15:17:10 [S0] agent.conversation_compression: context compression started: session=S0 messages=1618 tokens=~503,266   # second, independent compression on S0
15:20:03 [S2] agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=S2 messages=1618->1162
15:20:16 [S2] gateway.run: Session split detected: S0 → S2 (compression)
...
15:22:15 [S0] agent.conversation_compression: context compression started: session=S0 messages=1629 tokens=~504,601   # third, independent compression on S0
15:28:40 [S3] agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=S3 messages=1631->1161
15:29:02 [S3] gateway.run: Session split detected: S0 → S3 (compression)
```

Resulting `sessions` rows (SQLite `state.db`):

```text
S0  parent=<root>          end_reason=compression  ended_at=<time of FIRST split only>
S1  parent=S0              (2 min of content, dead end)
S2  parent=S0              (3 min of content, dead end)
S3  parent=S0              (the actual live continuation — 5+ hours of subsequent traffic)
```

`S1`, `S2`, `S3` are all **siblings** of each other (all `parent_session_id = S0`), not a chain. Only `S3` is live; `S1`/`S2` are orphaned, silently wasted forks that a human browsing raw session rows would find confusing (three "children" of the same compression event).

`get_compression_tip()`'s tie-break (prefer the child with the most recent message timestamp) happens to pick the correct tip (`S3`) here, so the user-visible projection self-heals — but this is luck, not a guarantee, and it silently discards `S1`/`S2` transcript content from ever being reachable via the normal chain-walk.

## Root Cause

1. `agent/auxiliary_client.py` (fix for #23975) wraps the compression summary call in `aux_interrupt_protection`, so once a turn enters compression, **that compression cannot be aborted** by a later gateway interrupt — it always runs to completion and always performs its own session split when done. This part is working as intended.
2. `gateway/run.py`'s default `busy_input_mode == "interrupt"` (`GatewayRunner._load_busy_input_mode`, default when unconfigured) does **not** wait for an in-flight compression + its session-id propagation (`entry.session_id = agent_session_id; session_store._save()`) before dispatching the next queued/incoming message. It interrupts the current turn and immediately starts a fresh turn against whatever session id the routing entry currently holds — which, in a tight race, can still be the pre-split parent, since the compression that will eventually rotate it away is still running in another task/thread.
3. If that new turn on the stale parent *also* grows past the compression threshold before the first compression finishes (easy in a rapid multi-message burst, since both turns share the same swelling transcript), it independently enters its **own** protected, uncancellable compression on the same stale parent id, producing a second sibling. Repeat for a third message → a third sibling.
4. Because `SessionDB.end_session()` is first-write-wins (only updates `ended_at`/`end_reason` while `ended_at IS NULL`), only the *first* split's `ended_at` sticks on the shared parent; the second and third `end_session(S0, "compression")` calls are silent no-ops (harmless here since the reason is the same, but it does mean `ended_at` on `S0` reflects only the first of three real split events).

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- The `interrupt` busy-input mode should not start a new turn against a session id that has an in-flight, uninterruptible compression outstanding — it should wait for that critical section (and the resulting id rotation) to land first, then route the new message to the rotated child; or
- Context compression should itself check "is there already a compression in flight for this session id" and short-circuit/join the existing one instead of letting two independent compressions race on the same stale parent.

## Actual Behavior

A burst of 3+ rapid messages during an in-flight compression can produce 3 sibling one-shot compression forks from the same stale parent within ~15 minutes, instead of one clean linear chain. `get_compression_tip()`'s recency tie-break usually (but not guaranteed to) picks the right tip, masking the symptom from the end user while quietly stranding the sibling transcripts outside the normal chain walk.

## Related Issues

- #23975 (closed, fixed by #49928) — introduced the interrupt-immune compression critical section that is one half of this race.
- #25242 (closed) — same general "interrupt + preflight compression" interaction area, different specific symptom (auto-continue note persistence).

## Environment

- Gateway default config (`busy_input_mode` unset → defaults to `interrupt`)
- Platform: WeChat (weixin) gateway integration, long-running DM session
- `hermes-agent` commit: 65be0061e06d172694785d65ae8c9d989becd64b (2026-06-26)

## Proposed Fix Direction

1. Track "compression in flight" per session id (e.g. alongside `_running_agents`) and have the gateway's interrupt-mode dispatch wait for/join that specific critical section before building a new agent for the same routing key, instead of racing a brand-new turn against the pre-rotation id.
2. Alternatively, make preflight-compression-triggering idempotent: before starting a new compression, check whether the current session row already has a fresher, still-being-created child from a compression that started after this turn's context snapshot, and skip/rejoin rather than starting a second one.

### Bug Description

After a Windows reboot, the first Hermes startup may fail with:

Another gateway instance (PID xxxx) is already running

Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1)

Desktop boot failed

Even though no gateway process is actually running.

What I expected

After reboot, Hermes should start a fresh gateway normally.

What actually happened

Hermes refused to start because it believed an old gateway instance was still running.

### Steps to Reproduce

Start Hermes gateway on Windows 11.

Shut down the PC without a planned Hermes stop.

Ensure gateway_state.json still contains the previous PID and gateway_state="running".

Reboot Windows.

Start Hermes Desktop (or let the VBS auto-start script launch the gateway).

Observed result

Another gateway instance (PID xxxx) is already running

Backend exits with code 1

Desktop enters a repair/retry loop

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should detect that the previous gateway process is gone and start a new gateway normally.

### Actual Behavior

Another gateway instance (PID 16428) is already running

Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1)

Desktop boot failed

Additional symptom

The Desktop UI shows "Gateway not started" and retries repeatedly.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/Gf1IT
  agent.log    https://paste.rs/ROQi1
  gateway.log  https://paste.rs/JGwQX
  gui.log      https://paste.rs/tOYyl
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

Python 3.11.x

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19) · upstream a658f3b2 

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Root Cause

The issue appears to be in gateway/status.py.

Relevant code path

get_running_pid()

get_runtime_status_running_pid()

_record_matches_live_gateway_pid()

Current logic

if live_cmdline:

... strict validation ...

return _record_looks_like_gateway(record)

Why it fails on Windows

gateway_state.json contains yesterday's PID and argv.

Windows can reuse PIDs after reboot.

psutil.cmdline() may raise AccessDenied or return None.

The fallback path checks only the recorded argv.

The stale record therefore looks like a valid gateway and blocks startup.

Result

Stale runtime record

PID recycled

cmdline unreadable

fallback(argv)

False positive: "gateway already running"

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Suggested change

When live_cmdline is unavailable, require the recorded start_time to match the PID's current start_time before trusting the record.

recorded_start = record.get("start_time")

current_start = _get_process_start_time(pid)

if recorded_start is not None and current_start is not None and recorded_start == current_start:

return _record_looks_like_gateway(record)

return False

Why this is safe

Safer failure mode

A false negative (starting a new gateway when the old one cannot be verified) is safer than a false positive that permanently prevents startup.

items.title: [Bug] gateway-locks PermissionError when HOME=/root and gateway runs as non-root UID (silently pauses Telegram)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery

items.body:
## Describe the bug

When Hermes gateway is started in a non-root container (e.g. UID 501) but `HOME=/root` is inherited from the container init context (`cont-init.d`), the gateway cannot write platform lock files and silently pauses dependent subsystems (e.g. Telegram integration).

## Environment

- Linux container (aarch64) running as non-root UID (e.g. 501)
- Gateway started via reconciler/`container_boot` which inherits `HOME=/root` from s6/cont-init context
- `HOME=/root` is not writable by UID 501

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run hermes-agent container as non-root UID with default `HOME=/root` (common in Docker with user remapping, or macOS bind-mount scenarios)
2. Gateway starts — appears running
3. Check logs: `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/<name>.lock'`
4. Telegram (or other subsystem) paused indefinitely with no user-facing error

## Expected behavior

Gateway writes lock files to a path writable by the running UID. If `HOME` is not writable, either fall back to a writable path (`HERMES_HOME` / `XDG_STATE_HOME`) or emit a clear startup error.

## Actual behavior

Gateway inherits `HOME=/root` from the init context. The lock path resolves to `/root/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/` — not writable as non-root. Gateway silently fails to acquire locks; Telegram connection pauses with no actionable log message.

## Root cause

The lock path is derived from `HOME` via `platformdirs` (or equivalent). The reconciler-launched gateway inherits the init-context environment where `HOME=/root`. As UID 501, writing to `/root/.local/` is denied.

Workaround: ensure `HOME` is set to a writable directory before launching the gateway:

```bash
HOME=/opt/data gateway run
```

Lock then lands under `/opt/data/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/` — writable.

## Prior art

HOME-mismatch issues: #17144, #33913, #27250, #16480, #20539, #15718 — but none document the specific `gateway-locks` permission failure path or Telegram pause symptom.

## Suggested fix

- Gateway startup should validate `HOME` is writable (or check `XDG_STATE_HOME`) and emit a clear error / fall back before attempting lock acquisition
- `container_boot` / reconciler should explicitly set `HOME` to the configured `HERMES_HOME` before spawning the gateway subprocess

## Platform

Linux container (aarch64), non-root UID, `HOME=/root`

Same issue as #16473, just two more cache dirs with no cleanup.

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

When multiple sessions are active across different platforms (e.g. desktop/TUI + Telegram), session context can bleed between them. The model executes tool calls that belong to a different session's conversation, and the response is routed to the wrong platform.

## Reproduction

1. Have an active session in the desktop/TUI (e.g. discussing "sessions" configuration).
2. Have a separate active session on Telegram (e.g. discussing "World Cup" results).
3. Finish the desktop session's task (e.g. creating a GitHub issue).
4. Observe that the model executes an unsolicited `web_search` for World Cup results **in the desktop session**, then routes the response to Telegram — even though no message was sent from Telegram.

## Evidence

Session `20260701_204935_30c298` (titled "sessions", source=tui, created in desktop app):

```log
2026-07-01 22:09:18,194 INFO [20260701_204935_30c298] tools.web_tools: Web search via tavily: 'World Cup results today July 2 2026' (limit: 5)
2026-07-01 22:09:19,999 INFO [20260701_204935_30c298] agent.tool_executor: tool web_search completed (1.83s, 1996 chars)
2026-07-01 22:09:32,238 INFO [20260701_204935_30c298] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=text_response model=qwen3.6-plus
2026-07-01 22:09:32,336 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=telegram chat=7358697584 time=132.5s
2026-07-01 22:09:32,370 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Sending response (652 chars) to 7358697584
```

The model called `web_search('World Cup results today July 2 2026')` **inside the "sessions" session**, then sent the response to Telegram. The user was not chatting about World Cup in this session — that context belongs to a **separate** Telegram session about the World Cup.

The user confirmed: **no message was sent from Telegram at that time**. They were just reading a previous reply.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The session routing index (`sessions.json`) maps `agent:main:telegram:dm:7358697584` → `30c298` (the "sessions" session). But the "world cup" session is also associated with the same Telegram user. When the agent loop finishes a task in one session, it may be pulling pending context from the other session due to:

1. **Shared gateway routing** — both sessions map to the same Telegram user ID
2. **Context bleed during API call** — the model receives mixed context from both sessions
3. **Unsolicited tool execution** — the model decides to "help" with the world cup topic using this session's tools

## Impact

1. **Wrong session answers.** Users get responses to questions they didn't ask in the current session.
2. **Tool call leakage.** Tool calls meant for one session execute in another.
3. **Platform routing confusion.** Responses from a desktop session get sent to Telegram (or vice versa).
4. **Privacy concern.** Context from one conversation bleeds into another.

## Environment

- Windows 11, Hermes `main` (commit `1d6645b`)
- Sessions: desktop/TUI + Telegram gateway active simultaneously
- Model: `qwen3.6-plus` via `opencode-go`

## Related

This may be related to issue #56439 (gateway `/resume` overwrites `sessions.source`), as both involve session identity and cross-platform routing confusion.

items.body:
## Bug Description

`ProviderProfile.fetch_models()` buffers the entire `/models` response with `resp.read().decode()` before JSON parsing. This path is used by live model catalog fetches for provider/model selection and doctor-style probes. A misconfigured proxy or hostile provider endpoint can return an unexpectedly large JSON/error body and make Hermes allocate the full response before falling back to static models.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure any provider profile whose live catalog URL points at an endpoint that advertises or streams a very large `/models` response.
2. Trigger a live model catalog fetch through provider/model selection or a direct `ProviderProfile.fetch_models()` call.
3. Observe that the current code performs an unbounded `resp.read()` before deciding whether to fall back.

## Expected Behavior

Live provider catalogs are advisory. Hermes should cap catalog responses and return `None` on oversized bodies so callers can fall back to the static model list.

## Actual Behavior

Hermes reads the full response body into memory before parsing JSON or failing.

## Affected Component

Configuration (provider/model catalog), CLI model selection, provider health/catalog probes.

## Proof

A focused local proof against `ProviderProfile.fetch_models()` confirms the capped behavior needed for the fix:

- oversized `Content-Length` returns `None` without calling `read()`
- missing `Content-Length` reads with a bounded `limit + 1` size instead of unbounded `read()`

## Issue: Windows subprocess console flashes — request for official fix

### Problem Summary

On Windows, Hermes spawns many subprocesses (npm, git, Python scripts, cron tasks, etc.). Each one briefly flashes a black console window. This is especially jarring when running in the background (cron jobs, code execution, etc.).

**Screenshot / Gif:** (attach if you have one showing the flash)

---

### Root Cause

Hermes only suppresses console windows in a **few specific call sites** via `creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW`:

- `tools/code_execution_tool.py`
- `tools/environments/local.py`

But **many other subprocess calls** (e.g., Node.js shims, npm, cron script execution, general CLI tools) do **not** set this flag, causing visible console flashes on every spawn.

---

### Proposed Fix (Patch Attached)

I wrote a patch that **globally injects** `CREATE_NO_WINDOW | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` into all `subprocess.Popen` and `subprocess.run` calls that don't explicitly set `creationflags`.

**Key changes:**

| File | Change | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` | Add `patch_subprocess_no_window()` | Global monkey-patch that injects `CREATE_NO_WINDOW \| CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` |
| `hermes_bootstrap.py` | Call `patch_subprocess_no_window()` on import | Ensures every Hermes process (main, cron, ACP adapter) gets the fix automatically |
| `cron/scheduler.py` | Use `pythonw.exe` instead of `python.exe` for cron scripts | `pythonw.exe` never allocates a console window, even `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` can't fully suppress it |
| `tools/code_execution_tool.py` | Add `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` to existing flags | Prevents child processes from inheriting the parent job object (needed for proper cleanup) |
| `tools/environments/local.py` | Same as above | Consistent behavior across all environments |

**Patch file:** `cron-pythonw-fix.patch` (see below)

```diff
# Full diff is in the patch file below; key snippet:

+def patch_subprocess_no_window() -> None:
+    """Globally monkey-patch subprocess.run/Popen to inject CREATE_NO_WINDOW
+    | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB on Windows when creationflags is not set."""
+    if not IS_WINDOWS:
+        return
+    import subprocess as _sp
+    _HIDE = _CREATE_NO_WINDOW | _CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB
+    _orig_run = _sp.run
+    _orig_popen = _sp.Popen
+    def _patched_run(*args, **kwargs):
+        if "creationflags" not in kwargs:
+            kwargs["creationflags"] = _HIDE
+        return _orig_run(*args, **kwargs)
+    def _patched_popen(*args, **kwargs):
+        if "creationflags" not in kwargs:
+            kwargs["creationflags"] = _HIDE
+        return _orig_popen(*args, **kwargs)
+    _sp.run = _patched_run
+    _sp.Popen = _patched_popen
```

---

### ⚠️ Critical Bug Found & Fixed During Implementation

**The first version of the patch caused a startup crash.** Here's what happened and why the **fixed version** must be used:

1. `hermes_bootstrap.py` is the **very first** module imported in every Hermes entry point.
2. The original patch called `patch_subprocess_no_window()` **before** `import asyncio`.
3. `patch_subprocess_no_window()` replaces `subprocess.Popen` (a **class**) with a **plain function**.
4. Python's standard library `asyncio/windows_utils.py` line 125 contains: `class Popen(subprocess.Popen):` — this **requires** `subprocess.Popen` to be a class.
5. When `asyncio` is later imported, it crashes with:

```
TypeError: function() argument 'code' must be code, not str
```

Or in some versions:
```
NameError: name 'base_events' is not defined
```

**✅ Fix:** Import `asyncio` (and `asyncio.coroutines`) **before** calling `patch_subprocess_no_window()`, so the stdlib gets the real `subprocess.Popen` class first. The patched function only affects **subsequent** calls.

```python

    import asyncio
    import asyncio.coroutines
    from hermes_cli._subprocess_compat import patch_subprocess_no_window
    patch_subprocess_no_window()
except Exception:
    pass
```

- **OS:** Windows 10 / 11
- **Hermes version:** (latest after `hermes update`)

### Why This Matters (Severity)

1. **UX degradation:** Every cron job, every npm call, every CLI tool flashes a console window. On a busy Hermes session this can happen dozens of times per minute.

### Summary

Refreshing Nous Portal account entitlements reads the `/api/oauth/account` response with an unbounded `resp.read()`. A malformed or unexpectedly large portal response can be fully buffered before Hermes validates that it is JSON.

### Affected path

- `hermes_cli/nous_account.py::_fetch_nous_account_info`
- Triggered when Hermes falls back from JWT claims to the fresh Nous Portal account API.

### Expected behavior

The account refresh path should read at most a bounded amount of response data and reject oversized bodies before JSON parsing.

### Actual behavior

The current code calls `resp.read().decode()` directly, so the response body is buffered without a size cap.

### Proof

Focused local proof replaced `urllib.request.urlopen` with fake responses:

- normal JSON response was parsed while `read()` was called with `1048577` bytes
- oversized `1048577` byte response raised `_NousAccountResponseTooLarge`
- `python -m py_compile hermes_cli\nous_account.py tests\hermes_cli\test_nous_account.py` passed

### Duplicate check

Checked open and closed PRs/issues for `nous account response cap`, `account usage response cap`, and related body-cap terms. Existing account-usage work covers a different usage endpoint; no open PR or issue was found for `/api/oauth/account`.

items.body:
## Description

Running `/journey` as a slash command (in both TUI and Desktop chat views) outputs raw ANSI 24-bit color escape codes instead of rendered/styled text. The ANSI codes appear as literal garbage (e.g. `?[38;2;...m`) in chat bubbles.

## Reproduction

1. Open Hermes TUI or Hermes Desktop
2. Type `/journey` and send it as a slash command
3. Observe output — the colored bar chart and node list render as raw ANSI escape sequences

Note: `hermes journey` from a real terminal/shell works correctly. The issue is specific to the slash-command execution path through the gateway.

## Root Cause

`tui_gateway/slash_worker.py` line ~155 creates a Rich Console with `force_terminal=True`:

```python
cli.console = Console(file=buf, force_terminal=True, width=120)
```

This unconditionally generates ANSI color codes in the captured output. The captured string is returned as plain text through the gateway to the client (TUI or Desktop), and neither the TUI chat view nor the Desktop chat view renders ANSI codes — they display output in a chat bubble element that treats escape sequences as literal text.

## Impact

Any slash command that produces rich terminal output through the CLI pipeline will have the same problem. Currently `/journey` is the most visible example.

## Related

Same class of bug as #4128 (`/tools list` shows raw escape codes), which was fixed by commit `9de4a38ce` by adding a `_TTYBuf` helper scoped to `_handle_tools_command()`. That fix only covered `/tools list`; the general slash-worker `_run()` path was not included.

## Suggested Fix

Either:

1. In `slash_worker.py:_run()`, strip ANSI codes from the captured output before returning it (~3 line change using `re.sub`)
2. Or detect that the consumer is a chat bubble (non-TTY) and pass `no_color=True` to the Rich Console

## Environment

- Hermes version: v0.17.0 (current main)
- Platform: Linux (Zorin OS / GNOME Wayland)
- TUI and Desktop both affected

labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Description

When a profile uses a `custom:` provider (e.g., `custom:token.sensenova.cn`), Hermes calls `clear_model_endpoint_credentials()` to remove the stale `model.api_key` field from the config. However, the YAML serializer writes the removed value back as `0` (YAML integer) instead of `""` (empty string).

Python's YAML parser then returns `api_key = 0` (int, falsy), which causes:
- `bool(0)` → `False` → `if not api_key:` checks short-circuit incorrectly
- `str(0)` → `"0"` is sent as `Authorization: Bearer ***` → all model API calls fail with 401

This affects all profiles using `custom` providers and can cascade — three config corruptions occurred in a single two-hour window as Hermes repeatedly tried and failed to save config after each model failure.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a `custom:` provider (e.g. in `config.yaml`):
   ```yaml
   model:
     provider: custom:my-provider
   ```
2. Start a Hermes session
3. Check `config.yaml` after startup — observe:
   ```yaml
   model:
     api_key: 0       # ← YAML integer, NOT string
   ```
4. Any model API call fails because `Bearer 0` is sent as auth header

## Root Cause

In `hermes_cli/config.py`, `clear_model_endpoint_credentials()` correctly pops the `api_key` key from the dict:
```python
model_cfg.pop("api_key", None)
```

But when the config is saved back to YAML, PyYAML's `dump()` serializes `None` as `0` (integer) when the field is explicitly written back as part of the full config tree. The fix should ensure that if `api_key` is written, it's always `""` (empty string) rather than `0` or `null`.

## Impact

- **All profiles** using `custom:` providers are affected
- Affects v0.17.0 (upstream 184c10cf)
- All 4 profiles on the reporter's system had this bug simultaneously
- Can cascade: repeated model failures → repeated config save → corrupted YAML

## Suggested Fix

Two possible approaches:
1. In `clear_model_endpoint_credentials()`, set `model_cfg["api_key"] = ""` instead of leaving the field removed (so YAML dump sees a string)
2. In the YAML save path, ensure `null`/`None` values for string fields are serialized as `""` not `0`

**Workaround per profile:**
```bash
hermes config set model.api_key ""
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19), commit 184c10cf
- Linux, multiple profiles with `custom:` provider
- All 4 profiles (default, memoirs, erp, tourism) affected

items.title: MCP stdio resolution ignores env PATHEXT on Windows

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, stdio MCP command resolution uses the configured MCP subprocess `env.PATH`, but extension lookup still depends on the parent process `PATHEXT`. If an MCP server config supplies a custom `PATHEXT` together with its `PATH`, Hermes can fail to resolve a valid command before starting the MCP subprocess.

## Affected path

- `tools/mcp_tool.py::_resolve_stdio_command`

The resolver calls `shutil.which(command, path=env[PATH])`. On Windows, `shutil.which(..., path=...)` still reads executable extensions from the current process environment, not from the MCP subprocess env. That makes `PATH` and `PATHEXT` inconsistent for stdio MCP startup.

## Expected behavior

When a stdio MCP config provides both `PATH` and `PATHEXT`, command resolution should use both values from that same env, including common Windows casing such as `Path` / `Pathext`.

## Actual behavior

A command can remain unresolved even though the configured MCP env can locate it by `PATH` + `PATHEXT`. The later stdio startup then receives a bare command name instead of the resolved executable path.

## Proof

Focused local proof on Windows:

```text
process PATHEXT = .EXE
MCP env PATH = <temp>\\bin
MCP env PATHEXT = .CMD
<temp>\\bin\\demo.cmd exists
_resolve_stdio_command(demo, env) should resolve demo.cmd
```

After the fix branch, the focused proof passes for both uppercase and Windows-style mixed-case env names:

```text
focused MCP PATHEXT proof passed
```

Additional verification:

```text
python -m py_compile tools\\mcp_tool.py tests\\tools\\test_mcp_tool_issue_948.py
```

`python -m pytest tests\\tools\\test_mcp_tool_issue_948.py -q` could not run in this checkout because pytest is not installed (`No module named pytest`).

## Scope

This is limited to stdio MCP command resolution. It does not change terminal command approval, shell execution policy, or non-Windows resolution behavior.
